item.title: Unpaid fines? Here’s who can save you from prison
item.description: Freiheitsfonds has raised almost 100'000 francs.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Freiheitsfonds has raised nearly 100'000 francs. - 47 people have avoided a total of 451 days in prison. - In 2024, there were 3'935 admissions for substitute sentences. - Substitute detention can last up to 90 days. ## Key facts - Fund → Freiheitsfonds - Funds raised → almost 100'000 francs - Beneficiaries → 47 people - Detention avoided → 451 days - Conversion → up to 90 days of detention - 2024 figure → 3'935 prison admissions - Zurich study → 69% for traffic or public transport violations - Estimated cost → 200-300 francs per day Data from the Federal Statistical Office indicate that in 2024, prison admissions in Switzerland for the enforcement of substitute sentences totaled 3'935, more than four times the number recorded in 2000. This figure highlights the problem addressed by Freiheitsfonds, the Swiss fund that pays the penalties of people who cannot afford them. Donations enabled the fund to raise almost 100'000 francs, which has already paid the penalties of 47 people. In total, the intervention avoided 451 days of detention, according to the NZZ. ### How substitute sentences work Failure to pay a fine or monetary penalty may lead to its conversion into a substitute custodial sentence lasting up to 90 days. This is a controversial mechanism, since it risks disproportionately affecting people facing financial difficulties and contributes to filling prisons. According to a study conducted in Zurich in 2019, 69% of those interviewed had received a penalty for violations related to traffic or public transport. In Parliament, the National Council rejected the proposal by Jessica Jaccoud, a Vaud Socialist National Councillor, which aimed to replace detention for unpaid fines of up to 5'000 francs with other measures. The fund believes that intervening before imprisonment is also economically worthwhile: according to the estimates cited, a day in detention costs 200-300 francs. The issue nevertheless continues to raise doubts. There are fears that intervention by a private party could weaken the enforcement of penalties and the deterrent effect of fines; moreover, people who travel without a ticket may not do so exclusively for financial reasons. Among the alternatives already provided for is community service, the organization of which can nevertheless prove complex. Zurich has a dedicated service; Bern, by contrast, wants to extend the use of this measure to cases in which the sentence has already been converted into detention. Finally, some municipalities suggest not filing criminal complaints against people who travel without a valid ticket, focusing instead on the surcharge and debt recovery. ## Three paths with different effects For people living in Switzerland, the issue is not limited to the amount of the penalty. The source compares three paths: conversion into substitute detention, community service and, in some cases of travelling without a valid ticket, a surcharge and debt recovery instead of a criminal complaint. ### The practical comparison | Path | What it entails according to the source | |---|---| | Unpaid fine or monetary penalty | Possible conversion into a substitute custodial sentence of up to 90 days | | Community service | An alternative already provided for, but not always easy to organize | | Travel without a valid ticket | In some municipalities, foregoing a criminal complaint, a surcharge and debt recovery | The first path is the one that turns non-payment into possible detention. The second keeps the response in the realm of community service, but applying it requires an organizational setup that the source describes as not always easy. The third concerns a narrower scope: travel without a valid ticket and proposals from some municipalities. The difference between the three paths has an immediate practical effect. According to its objective, the Freiheitsfonds intervenes before incarceration; community service is indicated as an alternative; the municipal transport model instead focuses on the surcharge and debt recovery. They are different responses to the same problem of non-payment, but they are not interchangeable. ### Where Zurich and Bern fit in Zurich has a service dedicated to community service. In Bern, the aim is to extend the use of this measure to sentences already converted into detention. The source therefore presents an existing service and an announced extension, not a single procedure described for all territories. From an economic perspective, the fund argues that intervention before detention makes sense because one day in prison is estimated to cost between 200 and 300 francs. As for the concerns, there remains a fear that a private entity could weaken enforcement of sanctions and reduce the deterrent effect of fines. The same source points out that financial difficulties do not necessarily explain every journey without a ticket. The practical picture therefore requires distinguishing between the type of sanction, the point at which conversion takes place, and the alternative provided for in the territory in question. A municipal transport proposal is not equivalent to private payment of a sanction, while community service is not the same as substitute detention. ## Navigating without adding unmentioned rules The source does not describe a single form, deadline or office for requesting assistance from the Freiheitsfonds. The practical steps that can therefore be reconstructed are linked to the type of sanction and the stage the case has reached. ### Four steps 1. Distinguish the sanction. The text considers both the fine and the monetary penalty. When they are not paid, they can be converted into a substitute custodial sentence, up to 90 days. 2. Place the case before imprisonment. The fund’s stated objective is to pay the sanctions of people at risk of prison because they cannot afford them. The source documents assistance for 47 people, but does not describe a general access procedure: it is therefore not possible to derive a form or deadline from the text. 3. Consider community service: the system already provides for it, but its organization is not always simple. The example cited is Zurich, which has a dedicated service; Bern aims to extend this option to sentences already converted into detention. 4. Separate public transport cases. For people travelling without a valid ticket, some municipalities propose waiving the criminal complaint and focusing on the surcharge and debt recovery. The proposal is linked to that type of offence and should not automatically be extended to every fine. ### The limits of the available information The text does not indicate a uniform procedure throughout Switzerland, nor does it establish that the fund pays every unpaid sanction. Instead, it reports an objective, some results and alternatives located in Zurich, Bern or unspecified municipalities. For the reader, the decisive distinction is therefore between an unpaid sanction, possible conversion, community service and the municipal model applied to travelling without a valid ticket. For more information on the everyday use of mezzi pubblici. *Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/cronaca/1956740/multe-non-pagate-ecco-chi-puo-salvarvi-dal-carcere)*

item.title: Switzerland, consultation on the WTO e-commerce agreement
item.description: Plurilateral Agreement on Electronic Commerce at the WTO 67 members, including Switzerland, choose provisional implementation Consultation from 14 October 2026
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Plurilateral Agreement on Electronic Commerce at the WTO - 67 members, including Switzerland, choose provisional implementation - Consultation from 14 October 2026 to 28 January 2027
## Key facts - Subject: plurilateral agreement on electronic commerce - Negotiations: concluded in 2024 within the WTO - Decision: 28 March 2026, 14th ordinary session - Participants: 67 members, including Switzerland - Instrument: Annex on provisional provisions - Objective: to simplify digital trade and strengthen legal certainty - Start of consultation: 14 October 2026 - Consultation deadline: 28 January 2027
## The decision and the consultation
Switzerland will open a consultation on the plurilateral agreement on electronic commerce on 14 October 2026. The text concerns a negotiation conducted within the WTO and already completed in 2024. The opening is communicated by the Federal Department of Economy, Education and Research, indicated in the official communication.
On 28 March 2026, at the 14th (regular) session of the WTO Ministerial Conference, 67 members, including Switzerland, opted for the application of the Agreement through an Annex on provisional provisions. The initiative does not yet equate to the formal inclusion of the agreement in the WTO legal framework: for now, the provisional regime adopted by the members remains distinct from the legal milestone envisaged for the agreement.
### An agreement still in the integration phase
The objective remains the formal inclusion of the agreement in Annex 4 of the WTO Agreement. According to the communication, this step is currently blocked by some WTO members. For this reason, the text describes a provisional solution already chosen by the 67 participants and, in parallel, a broader legal objective that has not yet been achieved. Switzerland appears among the members who have decided on implementation via the annex on provisional provisions, while the formalization is indicated as still blocked.
The calendar allows us to distinguish three moments. Negotiations within the WTO concluded in 2024; on 28 March 2026 the 67 members decided on implementation through the Annex on Interim Provisions; the consultation starts on 14 October 2026. They are different passages, with different functions in the text: the first concerns the end of the negotiations, the second the provisional arrangement, the third the time window communicated for the Swiss consultation. The consultation ends on 28 January 2027.
For those observing the Swiss economy, the concrete point indicated by the source is the objective of simplifying digital trade between members and, at the same time, strengthening legal certainty. The communication does not announce new operational rules, amounts or obligations for businesses and consumers. Furthermore, it does not provide a timetable after 28 January 2027. The article can therefore record the consultation and its scope, without transforming it into a modification that has already entered into force. ## Effects to be read with caution
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the news should be read as an institutional step, not as the announcement of a new immediate fulfillment. The source talks about an agreement intended to simplify digital trade between members and strengthen legal certainty, but does not list specific operational changes for online sales. Without these details, it is not possible to derive a new obligation for a Swiss operator from the communication.
### The value of distinction
The practical utility of news lies in separating what is already decided from what remains a goal. The decision of the 67 members concerns the implementation through an annex on the provisional provisions. The formal integration in Annex 4 of the WTO Agreement is instead described as still blocked by some WTO members. For a company that follows digital trade, this difference prevents it from presenting the agreement as a framework definitively integrated into the WTO system.
The source does not quantify the expected benefit and does not indicate which sectors, business size or categories of users would be involved first. The only declared effect is the general direction: to make digital trade between members easier and to increase legal certainty. Any assessment of costs, time, documents or procedures would require elements that do not appear in the communication.
### The comparison between the scenarios
The scenario described today combines a provisional implementation decision and a formal integration still blocked. If the block indicated by the source remained, the text would continue to distinguish these two planes; if the formal integration was achieved, the stated objective would have a different outcome. However, the source does not allow to attribute a date or a result to either scenario.
For this reason, the deadline of 28 January 2027 is above all the point of control of the consultation. It is not presented as the date of entry into force of the agreement, nor as the term for a new commercial obligation. Those working on Swiss digital exchanges can use this distinction to avoid premature conclusions. ## Follow the procedure:
Those who want to follow the consultation can start from an essential chronology, without overlapping the stages. The communication provides the dates, the object and the objective of the dossier. For any contributions, you must follow the instructions of the official documentation associated with the consultation; the article does not allow you to add channels or forms not indicated.
### Five operational checks
1. Identify the subject: plurilateral agreement on electronic commerce, negotiated within the framework of the WTO. 2. Rebuild the previous step: the negotiations were completed in 2024. 3. Record the decision of 28 March 2026: 67 members, including Switzerland, chose implementation by means of an annex on interim provisions. 4. Verify the perimeter: the objective remains the formal integration in Annex 4 of the WTO Agreement, currently blocked by some WTO members. 5. Mark the Swiss window: start on 14 October 2026, end on 28 January 2027.
For those preparing an analysis or intending to participate in the consultation, the most prudent line is to focus on the two stated objectives: simplifying digital trade between members and strengthening legal certainty. The material provided does not authorize to present as already defined new rates, forms, obligations, sanctions or deadlines other than January 28, 2027. Nor does it allow you to describe the formal integration as already approved.
After the end, the source does not indicate a date for the next step. The control to be done is therefore concrete: check if the official documentation associated with the consultation adds procedural instructions and follow any further communications on integration into the WTO. Until then, the verifiable basis remains the provisional decision of the 67 members and the consultation opened in Switzerland. This method makes it possible to distinguish a consultation deadline from an application date, a distinction that the text of the news item maintains.

item.title: Federal Council launches consultation on customs ordinances
item.description: The Federal Council launches the consultation on October 14, 2026 The project concerns the total revision of customs law The consultation deadline.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Federal Council launches the consultation on October 14, 2026 - The project concerns a total revision of customs law - The consultation period ends on January 28, 2027 - The focus is the new ordinance on the tasks of the UDSC
## Key facts - What → Total revision of customs law - Who → Federal Council - When → October 14, 2026 - Deadline → January 28, 2027 - Legal bases → LUDSC and LTDo - Program → DaziT - Parliament → June 20, 2025
The Federal Council launched the consultation procedure on October 14, 2026, at its meeting in Bern, on the package of ordinances for the total revision of customs law. The decision concerns the comprehensive modernization of the legal bases and forms part of the DaziT digitalization and transformation program, also linking to the development of the organization of the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (UDSC).
### A new framework ordinance
The core of the project is the creation of a new framework ordinance: the ordinance on the tasks of the UDSC. The text aims to reduce the administrative burden for the economy and clarify the methods for harmonizing and digitalizing procedures. Simplifications are also planned for the collection of duties and for the activities through which the UDSC manages and controls the cross-border movement of goods and people.
The federal communication therefore presents a framework that combines organization, procedures and duties. The package is intended to give concrete form to the new customs legislation through several implementing acts. The consultation concerns the preliminary drafts and the documentation published for the recipients identified in the procedure.
### The ordinances involved
Numerous ordinances are undergoing a total revision. The ordinance on customs will become the new ordinance on customs duties. The package also includes the ordinance on tobacco taxation, the ordinance on beer, the ordinance on motor vehicles, the ordinance on mineral oils and the ordinance on alcohol.
The timetable sets the close of the consultation for January 28, 2027. The amendments implement the LUDSC and the new LTDo through ordinances, adopted by Parliament on June 20, 2025. The LTDo governs customs duties, while the LUDSC consolidates and standardizes the UDSC's enforcement tasks in a single separate framework law.
The new provisions create the stated legal bases for simplifying, harmonizing and digitalizing customs and duty-collection processes on a large scale. The publication of October 14, 2026 accompanies the opening with the preliminary drafts, explanatory reports, a letter to the Cantons, a letter to organizations and the list of recipients of the procedure. ## What it means for procedures
For companies and operators handling goods or people across the border, the most concrete point indicated by the Federal Council is not a new amount, but how the procedures should be organized. The source links the new ordinance to three objectives: reducing the administrative burden, harmonizing the steps and digitizing the procedures. These objectives are aimed at the economy and the UDSC's activities. However, the press release does not indicate figures, rates or savings timelines.
This limitation is relevant to a practical reading of the dossier. The text announces a total revision and puts preliminary drafts out for consultation, but does not present a list of new obligations to be fulfilled immediately. The most prudent implication for those operating in cross-border traffic is therefore to distinguish between the project's stated direction and the applicable rules described in the press release.
### Comparison between the current and proposed frameworks
The comparison that can be made concerns primarily the structure of the rules. The legislation approved by Parliament separates the rules governing customs duties, contained in the LTDo, from the UDSC's implementation tasks, set out in the LUDSC. The package of ordinances reflects this distinction: the customs ordinance is transformed into an ordinance on customs duties, while a new framework ordinance specifies the office's tasks and the manner in which procedures are conducted.
| Scope | Reference cited | Project direction | |---|---|---| | Customs duties | LTDo and ordinance on customs duties | Revision of the implementing rules | | UDSC tasks | LUDSC and ordinance on the tasks of the UDSC | Harmonization through a framework law and the ordinances | | Processes | DaziT Programme | Digitalization, simplification and harmonization |
### What remains to be verified
The ordinances on the taxation of tobacco, beer, motor vehicles, mineral oils and alcohol are included in the package, but the press release does not indicate specific changes for each duty. The source therefore provides no new amounts or new rates to apply. The consultation is the step explicitly communicated and closes on January 28, 2027.
The dossier is also accompanied by a letter to the cantons, a letter to organizations and a list of recipients. These documents are part of the official publication together with the texts and explanatory reports. For families, workers and businesses, the concrete point is therefore the launch of a broad regulatory revision, with procedural effects still to be defined through the documents submitted for consultation. ## How to follow the consultation
To read the dossier in an orderly manner, the process can be organized into five steps based on the materials provided:
1. Mark January 28, 2027 as the deadline for the consultation procedure. 2. Open the draft ordinances published on October 14, 2026. 3. Read the explanatory reports on the total revision alongside the texts. 4. Consult the letter to the Cantons, the letter to the organizations and the list of recipients. 5. Compare the ordinances with the LUDSC and LTDo adopted by Parliament on June 20, 2025.
The first reading criterion is the subject of the dossier. For the tasks and controls of the UDSC, start with the ordinance on the tasks of the UDSC, that is, the new framework ordinance. For the regulation of customs duties, the reference is the ordinance on customs duties, intended to replace the Customs Ordinance as part of the total revision.
A second approach concerns specific levies. The package includes texts relating to tobacco, beer, motor vehicles, mineral oils and alcohol. It is therefore advisable to associate each topic with the relevant draft ordinance and corresponding explanatory report, without confusing these ordinances with the general ordinance on the tasks of the UDSC.
The documentation is presented in separate archives: the draft ordinances are provided in a 5.01 MB ZIP file, while the explanatory reports are collected in a 3.31 MB ZIP file. The same publication lists the documents addressed to the Cantons and organizations and makes the list of recipients of the procedure available.
For those following the dossier from the perspective of the economy or cross-border traffic, this sequence avoids reading a single ordinance in isolation. The DaziT program in fact links the digitalization, simplification and harmonization of customs and duty collection processes. The deadline indicated by the Federal Council remains January 28, 2027; until that date, the official material to be examined is that of the consultation launched on October 14, 2026.
*Source: [admin.ch](https://www.admin.ch/it/newnsb/Jmo3fhpgMuJt)*

item.description: Alliance Care closes and files for bankruptcy The decision was made in Bern 17 layoffs among 91 employees ASI had granted loans Organization →
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Alliance Care closes and initiates bankruptcy proceedings - The decision was made in Bern - 17 layoffs out of 91 employees - ASI had granted loans
## Key facts - Organization → Alliance Care - Decision → cessation of operations and bankruptcy proceedings - Founded → June 2025 - Staff → 91 employees; 17 laid off - Stabilization → efforts launched in April 2026 - Members → memberships below expectations - Support → loans from Associazione svizzera infermieri - Report → July investigation in Tamedia group newspapers
Alliance Care is ceasing its activities and initiating bankruptcy proceedings. In Bern, the nursing council and the assembly of delegates adopted the decision after an in-depth discussion.
The organization cites financial difficulties as the cause of the closure. Financial results were below expectations, and the measures launched in April 2026 to stabilize the accounts did not make it possible to ensure continuity of operations.
### A crisis that emerged in stages
In June, the first signs of the crisis had already emerged, with 17 of Alliance Care's 91 employees being laid off. Associazione svizzera infermieri, which promoted the project, had sought to provide financial support to the new organization through several loans. Despite this, the financial problems had not been resolved.
The failure to increase membership was another factor. Growth in new members was one of the foundations of the association's development prospects, but membership did not reach the hoped-for levels. Alliance Care thus became unable to ensure long-term financial stability. The difficulties affected both the accounts and the expected membership growth.
An investigation published last July by the newspapers of the Tamedia group had shown that membership was significantly below forecasts. This was part of the series of difficulties that culminated in today's decision.
Founded in June 2025, Alliance Care aimed to bring together in a single organization all professionals in the care sector, including healthcare workers without a nursing diploma. Just over a year after its founding, the representation project is closing with the initiation of bankruptcy proceedings. ## What it means for healthcare representation
The bankruptcy of Alliance Care brings to an end an organizational project designed to broaden the representation of healthcare personnel. The source links that project to two precise conditions: the ability to support the finances and the arrival of new members. When membership remained below expectations, the prospect of long-term financial stability disappeared.
### Before and after
Before the decision, Alliance Care was supposed to bring together under one roof all care professionals, including healthcare workers without a nursing diploma. After the decision of the nursing council and the assembly of delegates, that objective will not continue through the organization. For those working in the sector, the news should be read as the conclusion of a specific association model, not as a change to the professional activities described in the source.
The comparison can be summarized as follows: - the project aimed at broader representation; - the arrival of new members was part of the development prospects; - financial results and membership numbers did not reach the necessary levels.
This sequence also clarifies the role of the Swiss Nurses Association. As its promoter, ASI had granted loans to the new organization. The source specifies, however, that these measures were not enough to resolve the economic problems. The initial support, therefore, did not enable Alliance Care to achieve the financial stability it was seeking.
The figure for employees should be read without additions. The 17 layoffs out of 91 people are the number indicated for June, when the first signs of the crisis had already emerged. The text does not make it possible to infer any other employment outcomes, nor to establish what the position of the staff not involved in those layoffs will be.
For members as well, the source establishes one point, but does not describe subsequent steps: membership was below expectations and this affected long-term prospects. No methods of reimbursement, transfer, or continuation of individual memberships are indicated. The practical takeaway therefore remains limited to the end of the organization and the initiation of bankruptcy proceedings. ## What to do now
For anyone who has a direct relationship with Alliance Care, the first rule is to separate information already confirmed from consequences not yet described. The source permits a limited but concrete sequence of actions, without assigning deadlines or offices to the proceedings that are not indicated.
### A five-step check
1. Identify your relationship with the organization: member, employee, or professional interested in the representation project. These are the categories mentioned in the text and require different attention. 2. Consider Alliance Care's operations terminated, because the decision of the nursing council and the assembly of delegates was accompanied by the initiation of bankruptcy proceedings. 3. For anyone among the 91 employees mentioned, distinguish the figure of 17 dismissals from any forecast about the remaining staff. The source provides no further employment outcomes. 4. For members, do not take continuity of membership or any possible transfer for granted. The text links memberships to financial stability, but does not describe the arrangements following closure. 5. Keep the communications and await guidance related to the bankruptcy proceedings before making commitments. No deadlines, forms, or authorities to contact are reported; adding them would mean introducing extraneous information.
For care professionals who need to assess their employment path, employment figures should be kept separate from the market for available positions. The news report does not publish job offers, replacements, or placements for the staff involved.
Bankruptcy proceedings have been initiated, but the source does not provide an operational timetable. The most prudent action is therefore to check your own position and await communications formally relating to the case. It is not possible to indicate a deadline or a form based on the material provided. Anyone who needs to look for new employment can consult annunci di lavoro.

item.title: Swisscom fine annulled: COMCO assesses the appeal
item.description: The TAF annuls Swisscom’s 18,4 million fine.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - TAF annuls Swisscom's fine of 18,4 million francs - The penalty was imposed in December 2023 - COMCO is considering whether to appeal to the Federal Supreme Court
## Key facts - Subject → fiber-optic dispute - Penalty → 18,4 million francs - Date of penalty → December 2023 - COMCO investigation → launched at the end of 2020 - Next step → analysis of the ruling in the coming days - Possible outcomes → acceptance or appeal to the Federal Supreme Court
### The course of the dispute
18,4 million francs: that is the amount of the fine that the Federal Administrative Court annulled in the ruling made public yesterday evening. The penalty had been imposed on Swisscom in December 2023 and arose from the fiber-optic dispute.
The FAC did not find that the telecom operator held a dominant position. This conclusion differs from that of the Competition Commission, which had argued that there was a dominant position and had launched an investigation into the case at the end of 2020. That investigation then culminated in the penalty imposed in December 2023.
The central issue in the matter is therefore the interpretation of a dominant position in the telecommunications sector. On the one hand, there is COMCO's assessment, which led to the fine; on the other, that of the FAC judges, who did not recognize that position and annulled the penalty.
The proceedings do not necessarily end with the ruling made public yesterday evening. COMCO told the Awp news agency that it would examine the judgment in depth in the coming days. Only after this analysis will the authority decide how to proceed.
The two options indicated are clear-cut: accept the judgment of the Federal Administrative Court or appeal to the Federal Supreme Court. In the first case, COMCO accepts the FAC's decision. In the second, the fiber-optic dispute continues before the court indicated by the authority itself.
The report therefore describes one step that has already been decided and another that remains open. The decided step is the annulment of the fine of 18,4 million francs. The open one concerns the Competition Commission's response, expected after the analysis announced for the coming days. ## The practical takeaway for the telecom sector
The judgment has a concrete effect on the proceedings: the fine imposed on Swisscom in December 2023 has been annulled. Its significance, however, must be considered together with the decision that COMCO still has to make. The same dispute remains tied to two different interpretations of the dominant position in the telecom sector: the one supported by the authority and the one accepted by the Federal Administrative Court.
For people who live or work in Switzerland, the practical takeaway is not an already announced change to bills, contracts, plans, speeds or coverage. The source does not report changes of this kind. Automatically linking the annulment of the penalty to savings for users or a deterioration in service would therefore go beyond the available information.
### Two scenarios for the national perspective
The first scenario is acceptance of the judgment. In this case, COMCO would not file the appeal mentioned in the news report, and the case would remain governed by the TAF's judgment, which found that Swisscom did not hold a dominant position.
The second scenario is an appeal to the Federal Supreme Court. Here, the point to watch would not be a new fine already decided, but the continuation of the dispute over the interpretation of the dominant position and fiber optics. The source does not anticipate which option will be chosen or what the outcome of any appeal would be.
The difference between before and after the judgment is therefore primarily procedural. Before, COMCO's position had led to an investigation launched in late 2020 and to the penalty in December 2023. After the decision made public yesterday evening, that fine was annulled by the TAF, and the authority must consider its next step.
This is also the useful framework for interpreting any reactions in the telecommunications sector. The verified fact concerns the penalty, the dispute over fiber optics, and the interpretation of the dominant position. The source contains no figures on prices, investments, customers, or commercial terms. The national significance of the news is therefore tied to the process involving COMCO, TAF, and possible involvement of the Federal Supreme Court, not to an announced change in tariffs. ## How to follow the case without anticipating the outcomes
To correctly understand the next developments, it is useful to separate the outcome of the judgment from the decision still awaited from COMCO. The former is already known; the latter has yet to arrive.
### Monitoring procedure
1. Establish the current status: the Federal Administrative Court annulled the fine of 18,4 million francs imposed on Swisscom in December 2023.
2. Identify the subject: the matter concerns the dispute over fiber optics and the dominant position in the telecommunications sector. It should not be turned into an announcement about tariffs or services, because the source contains no indications of this kind.
3. Await the step indicated by COMCO: the authority said it will examine the judgment thoroughly in the coming days. No precise date is reported, so a different deadline should not be added.
4. Distinguish between the two outcomes: COMCO may accept the TAF's ruling or file an appeal with the Federal Supreme Court. These are the only avenues indicated in the report.
This framework also avoids a frequent error in reading the case: confusing the annulment of the sanction with the already definitive conclusion of every step. The TAF's judgment resulted in the annulment of the fine, but COMCO still has to announce whether it accepts the ruling or chooses to appeal.
The source does not indicate any forms to fill out, documents to submit, or obligations for residents and workers. There is therefore no individual procedure to initiate in order to follow the case. The concrete action consists of checking what decision the Competition Commission will make after the announced analysis and keeping the facts already established separate from any possible future consequences.
Until COMCO's choice is indicated, the information to use is that of the judgment made public last night: the fine was annulled, and the issue of the dominant position remains at the center of the dispute over fiber optics.

item.title: Switzerland participates in IMF and World Bank in Bangkok 2026
item.description: IMF and World Bank summit in Bangkok from October 15 to 17, 2026 Parmelin, Keller-Sutter and Schlegel in the Swiss delegation New partnership agreement
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - IMF and World Bank summit in Bangkok from October 15 to 17, 2026 - Parmelin, Keller-Sutter and Schlegel in the Swiss delegation - New Swiss partnership agreement with the IMF - 40 million francs to the IMF for the 2026–2030 period
## Key facts - Date of the communiqué → October 14, 2026 - Venue and dates → Bangkok, from October 15 to 17, 2026 - Participants → Guy Parmelin, Karin Keller-Sutter, Martin Schlegel - Partnership → approved by the Federal Council on August 26, 2026 - Amount → 40 million francs for the 2026–2030 period
On October 14, 2026, from Bern, the Confederation announced Switzerland’s participation in the annual meeting of the IMF and World Bank, scheduled to take place in Bangkok from October 15 to 17, 2026. The meeting will be attended by President of the Confederation Guy Parmelin, Federal Councillor Karin Keller-Sutter, and Martin Schlegel, President of the Swiss National Bank.
During the same summit, the G20 finance ministers will meet with central bank governors. The Swiss delegation will also use the opportunity to hold bilateral talks.
### The Confederation’s position
The meetings will address current global challenges facing the economy and development policy. The communiqué emphasizes that persistent geopolitical tensions and trade conflicts are weighing on the global economy. Switzerland is committed to reliable international economic relations, open markets and resilient supply chains.
The position also lists three conditions for resilience and growth: sound public finances, financial stability and integrity, as well as an economic policy conducive to innovation. With regard to the IMF, Switzerland calls for qualified and independent advice focused on fundamental risks and core competencies. It also supports comprehensive and objective assessments of member countries’ positions on external economic policy, prudent lending and sound Fund finances.
The World Bank is viewed positively for its greater focus on jobs and private investment. The stated priority remains development impact and the fight against poverty, with favorable economic framework conditions, effective and inclusive labor markets, and high environmental and social standards.
Finally, Switzerland will sign a new partnership agreement with the IMF; the Federal Council approved it on August 26, 2026. item.description: The Federal Council decides on October 14, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Federal Council will decide on October 14, 2026. - DETEC will prepare the dispatch by June 2027. - The reporting will cover all presumably illegal content.
## Key facts - Date → October 14, 2026 - Location → Bern - Project → Act on communication platforms and search engines (LPCom) - Assignment → DATEC - Deadline → end of June 2027 - Support → political parties, cantons, umbrella associations and national organizations - Cooperation → DFI and UFAS - Launch of the consultation → October 29, 2025
The preliminary draft must be supplemented with measures to protect young people. The reporting procedure must also be extended to all presumably illegal content. These are the two measures announced by the Federal Council after the consultation.
The project has garnered broad support, expressed by the majority of the parties represented in the Federal Assembly, the cantons, the umbrella associations and the national organizations. The dossier also refers to the press release of October 29, 2025 on the start of the consultation.
### Rules for large platforms The new LPCom aims to strengthen users' rights and require providers to be more transparent. The law would apply to major communication platforms and search engines, including AI-based search engines. Smaller services, however, would not be covered by the project.
Google, Facebook and YouTube are cited as examples of services that people turn to for information and to form an opinion. According to the press release, these platforms are increasingly influencing public debate.
The project provides that providers of communication platforms make available to users a simple procedure for reporting all presumably illegal content. In terms of youth protection, large platforms and search engines should assess the risks created or exacerbated by their services and adopt measures to reduce them. DATEC will be assisted by DFI and UFAS in drafting the provisions dedicated to young people. For those living in Switzerland, the decision mainly describes the direction the Federal Council intends future regulation to take. The press release refers to a preliminary draft and announces a dispatch from DETEC by the end of June 2027; it does not, however, announce the law's entry into force. The distinction is practical: the measures described belong to the project submitted for consultation and are not presented as obligations that are already applicable.
### Users and providers: the possible change If the project is taken forward in the indicated form, a user of a large communication platform will have a simple procedure for reporting presumably illegal content. The novelty therefore concerns the relationship between user and provider: the project gives importance to the possibility of reporting and to the transparency of the services.
| Scope | Effect described in the preliminary draft | |---|---| | User rights | Simple reporting procedure | | Transparency | Greater provider transparency | | Youth protection | Assessment and reduction of risks | | Advertising | Ban on profiling young people |
The scope of application is selective. The proposal concerns large communication platforms and search engines, while smaller services should not be included. The mention of AI-based search engines expands the topic beyond social networks alone: the way information is searched for online also falls within the regulation outlined by the Federal Council.
For young people, the project shifts the focus to the organization of services. Providers will be required to analyze the extent to which their platforms create or exacerbate risks and to implement mitigation measures. The stated objective is not only safer use, but also consideration of young people's right to participate in public debate.
The ban on advertising is formulated precisely: it concerns ads based on profiling, that is, on analysis of young people's online behavior and personal characteristics. The press release does not describe a general ban on advertising. For this reason, the concrete effect will depend on the provisions that will be included in the dispatch and on the subsequent legislative process. The dossier can be followed through four steps, without confusing the preliminary draft with an already defined law.
1. **Establish the institutional phase.** The reference date is 14 October 2026: at its meeting in Bern, the Federal Council took note of the results of the consultation and decided to retain the project, strengthening youth protection. This is the decision communicated; no date of entry into force is indicated.
2. Consult the document on the results. The official material includes the Report on the results of the consultation concerning the preliminary draft of the Federal Act on communication platforms and search engines, published on 14 October 2026. It is the reference indicated for reconstructing the positions that emerged during the procedure.
3. Note the next deadline. DETEC must prepare a dispatch by the end of June 2027. Those following federal politics can therefore check at that deadline how the provisions on reporting presumably unlawful content and youth protection will be formulated.
4. Separate the obligations by addressee. For users, the project provides for a simple reporting procedure with communication platform providers. For providers of large platforms and search engines, the text provides for risk assessment and mitigation measures. For young people, it also indicates a ban on profiling-based advertising. These elements should be read as measures of the preliminary draft until the dispatch has been prepared.
In preparing the rules on young people, DETEC will be supported by the Federal Department of Home Affairs, the FDHA, and the Federal Social Insurance Office, the FSIO. Their involvement is already indicated in the Federal Council's decision and represents the operational step planned to complete the project by the announced deadline.

item.title: Hiring in Switzerland: companies cautious despite GDP
item.description: Swiss NEO at +21% for October–December 2026 Global NEO +29%; European average +20% Swiss GDP growing by 1,5% in the second quarter of 2026 Junior: 35% more
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Swiss NEO at +21% for October–December 2026 - Global NEO +29%; European average +20% - Swiss GDP growing by 1,5% in the second quarter of 2026 - Junior: 35% more hires, 21% down
## Key facts - Period -> October-December 2026 - Seasonally adjusted NEO in Switzerland -> +21% - Global NEO -> +29% - European average -> +20% - Swiss GDP -> +1,5% in the second quarter of 2026 - Junior hiring on the rise -> 35% - Longer talent search -> 32% - AI-generated résumés -> 16%
In the fourth quarter of 2026, Switzerland's seasonally adjusted Net Employment Outlook (NEO) is +21%. The indicator for the October-December period improves by one percentage point compared with the previous quarter, but falls by four points year on year. For the third consecutive quarter, it remains at its lowest levels since 2022.
The international comparison confirms the cautious position: global NEO stands at +29%, eight points above that of the Confederation. The Swiss figure remains just above the European average, set at +20%.
### GDP and temporary employment point to a different picture
This is shown by a ManpowerGroup survey, reported by Keystone-ATS, which highlights the contrast between companies' caution and overall economic developments. In the second quarter of 2026, Swiss gross domestic product grew by 1,5% compared with the previous quarter: the strongest pace since 2021. Since the beginning of the year, the temporary employment market has also been growing, considered an indicator of future economic cycles.
> “Economic signals are more positive than companies' hiring intentions,” Eric Jeannerod, the multinational's head for Switzerland, said in a statement.
The manager explains that companies are assessing more cautiously which skills are needed, where new hires make sense in the long term, and how to use artificial intelligence after the initial enthusiasm.
The sectoral picture remains differentiated. Construction and industry continue to show a need for personnel; in other sectors, jobs with a high share of potentially automatable activities are under pressure. Recruitment is thus focused on specific qualifications and areas, rather than on uniform demand.
A positive signal comes from junior profiles. Compared with the previous year, hiring dynamics improve by 14 percentage points: 35% of managers surveyed report a slight or significant increase, while 21% indicate a decrease. For those entering the workforce, getting started remains challenging, but the change may suggest a reversal in the trend. ## Labour demand is split by skills
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the practical takeaway is not to choose between growth and crisis. The data describe demand moving in different directions: economic strength does not automatically lead to the same intensity of recruitment in every area. The focus becomes the relationship between the skills required and the skills that can be identified.
### The selection filter
32% of the managers surveyed say that finding suitable talent now takes longer than it did a year ago, while only 20% consider recruitment easier. The main difficulty identified by companies is candidates' lack of skills, cited by 43%. This is followed by the discrepancy between candidates' expectations and employers' demands, at 26%, and AI-generated résumés, identified by 16% as a factor that complicates the identification of suitable profiles.
For those looking for work, the message is concrete: an application must clearly show actual skills and how they relate to the work required. The source describes AI-optimized résumés and the like; an undifferentiated presentation risks not helping those doing the selecting distinguish abilities, qualifications, and potential. The problem, therefore, concerns not only how many positions are open, but how clearly demand and supply are able to meet.
### Two paths for those entering the workforce
The improvement in junior profiles opens a different path from that of roles exposed to automation. The annual increase of 14 percentage points signals an opening, but entering the workforce remains challenging. For a young person, the positive signal does not eliminate the need to demonstrate relevant skills; rather, it suggests that companies may assess artificial intelligence in a more differentiated way.
From the companies' perspective, the problem is not solved by choosing between a shortage and a surplus of labor. Demand and supply diverge in some areas, while companies must decide which skills are truly needed and which hires make sense in the long term. The development of existing employees and the recognition of potential beyond traditional paths thus become levers for selection and growth, alongside the search for new employees. ## From the snapshot to the operational decision
The period to mark is October–December 2026, the quarter covered by the forecast. To turn the national data into a decision, it is advisable to proceed by qualifications, activities and potential, without focusing solely on GDP trends.
### Five steps for job seekers
1. Mark the period: October–December 2026 is the forecast window. Use it as a time reference, not as an individual guarantee.
2. Start with the activity, not the general job title. The source points to staffing needs in construction and industry and recruitment focused on specific qualifications and areas. Compare your profile with those requirements.
3. Make your actual skills recognizable. AI-optimized CVs may look similar; therefore describe what you can do and the potential you can demonstrate.
4. If you are junior, consider the improvement in hiring as an opportunity, not a guarantee. Entering the workforce remains challenging, including through non-traditional paths.
5. If an application receives no response, review your profile in relation to the qualification and area chosen. 32% of managers report a longer search for talent: it is worth checking alignment, rather than interpreting every outcome as a general judgment on the market.
### Guidance for employers
For companies, the operational step is to assess which skills are really needed and whether a new hire is worthwhile in the long term. The caution identified by ManpowerGroup coexists with the demand cited for construction and industry: it makes that demand more selective. It is advisable to pair external recruitment with developing existing employees and assessing potential beyond traditional pathways. AI-generated CVs should also be read by distinguishing the profile text from the skills actually required.
A useful check separates the three difficulties identified by the survey: missing skills, at 43%; misaligned expectations and requirements, at 26%; AI-generated CVs, at 16%. For candidates, each item suggests a different check; for companies, it helps avoid confusing the difficulty of reading profiles with an absence of demand.
Those looking for a job can consult the aziende che assumono and use the qualifications framework as a selection criterion. To move from reading the market to searching for opportunities, consult the annunci di lavoro.

item.description: The Federal Council launches the consultation on ACE.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Federal Council launches the consultation on the ACE. - The agreement brings together 67 WTO members. - The consultation ends on 28 January 2027. - The ACE prohibits tariffs on electronic transmissions.
## Key facts - Start: October 14, 2026 - Deadline: January 28, 2027 - Agreement: plurilateral agreement on electronic commerce - Participants: 67 WTO members - Coverage: approximately 70 percent of world trade - Framework: shared international rules - Swiss party: Switzerland - Ministerial declaration: March 28, 2026
### The federal timetable
On October 14, 2026, in Bern, the Federal Council launched the consultation procedure on the plurilateral agreement on electronic commerce, referred to by the acronym ACE. The consultation will remain open until January 28, 2027. Through the ACE, 67 WTO members establish a common regulatory framework for electronic commerce; according to the press release, the agreement also strengthens legal certainty for businesses.
The 67 members of the World Trade Organization covered by the agreement collectively represent approximately 70 percent of world trade. Participants include the European Union and its Member States, Australia, China, Japan, Canada, Singapore, the United Kingdom and Switzerland. Since the agreement is plurilateral, accession remains open to all WTO members.
### The rules contained in the ACE
The press release presents the ACE as an instrument for facilitating cross-border digital trade in goods and services. The provision identified as central prohibits the application of customs duties to electronic transmissions. The agreement also promotes the recognition of electronic procedures and documents and the conduct of commercial transactions without paper-based support.
Provisions aimed at consolidating trust in digital trade include consumer protection, data protection and cybersecurity. The press release recalls that Switzerland participated in the negotiations from the outset and contributed to drafting the agreement. The country undertakes to promote modern rules for electronic commerce both bilaterally and within the EFTA framework. According to the communication, the ACE is consistent with the high standards pursued by Switzerland in its most recent trade agreements and takes Switzerland's interests into account, especially with regard to data protection.
The negotiations were substantively concluded in 2024. The Ministerial Declaration of March 28, 2026, provided for entry into force through an annex containing provisional provisions, while formal inclusion in the WTO legal framework remains a shared objective. ## The practical effect for Swiss companies
### Greater predictability in digital operations
For the Swiss economy, the impact of the ACE described here lies in the predictability of cross-border digital operations. The statement refers to trade in goods and services, more reliable framework conditions, and greater legal certainty. These are the elements that matter to a Swiss company when it operates in cross-border digital trade with one of the parties to the agreement.
The provision on tariffs has a precise scope: the source refers to the prohibition on imposing customs duties on electronic transmissions. Alongside this rule, the text indicates recognition of electronic procedures and documents. The third element is the possibility of conducting commercial transactions without paper documentation. Taken together, these points outline an exchange model based on digital procedures recognized among the participants.
In terms of trust, the agreement links e-commerce to consumer protection, data protection, and cybersecurity. They are not presented as aspects separate from trade: the statement identifies them as provisions intended to strengthen trust in the digital sphere. For Switzerland, data protection is also mentioned among the interests taken into account in the agreement.
### The competitive dimension
The statement attributes two specific outcomes for Switzerland to the ACE: preventing the country from being disadvantaged compared with the other contracting parties and improving competitive conditions for Swiss companies. The reference to the 67 members and to approximately 70 percent of world trade shows the international dimension of the regulatory framework.
The plurilateral structure keeps the agreement open to accession by all WTO members. This element broadens the scope envisaged by the text without turning it into an agreement limited to Switzerland or a single group of countries. The consultation now allows the dossier to be examined, while the objective, still shared by the participants, of formally including the ACE in the WTO legal framework remains separate. ## How to follow the consultation
### Four operational steps
Anyone following the e-commerce dossier can organize their reading of the Federal Council’s communication in four steps, without confusing the consultation timetable with the agreement’s process.
- Mark October 14, 2026 as the start date and January 28, 2027 as the consultation deadline. - Identify the scope: cross-border digital trade in goods and services among the 67 WTO members. - Examine the operational areas indicated by the ACE: electronic transmissions, electronic documents and procedures, paperless transactions. - Keep the provisional regime and the objective of formal inclusion in the WTO legal framework distinct.
The dossier unfolds over three time stages. The negotiations were substantively concluded in 2024. At the WTO’s 14th Ordinary Ministerial Conference, on March 28, 2026, 67 members issued a ministerial declaration in which they agreed to bring the ACE into force through an annex containing provisional provisions. Finally, on October 14, 2026, the Federal Council launched the consultation procedure.
For a Swiss company, the internal review can follow the same order. First, consider whether the activity falls within cross-border digital trade in goods and services. Then isolate operations based on electronic transmissions and examine the recognition of electronic documents and procedures. Finally, assess references to consumer protection, data protection and cybersecurity.
The Swiss position should be read together with the country’s participation in the negotiations and its commitment, also within the EFTA framework, to modern rules on e-commerce. For those who need to set a single deadline, the one indicated by the Federal Council is January 28, 2027.

item.description: Risks remain high in Switzerland The Federal Council takes note of the third report The GCRF makes eight recommendations More resources and sanctions are needed
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Risks remain high in Switzerland - The Federal Council takes note of the third report - The GCRF makes eight recommendations - More resources and stricter sanctions are needed
## Key facts - Document → third national risk report - Scope → money laundering and terrorist financing - Recommendations → eight - Authorities → GCRF - Objective of sanctions → «effective and dissuasive sanctions» - Register → transparency of beneficial owners, in force at the beginning of October
In Bern, the Federal Council took note of the Confederation's report on the threats posed to Switzerland by money laundering and terrorist financing. The document indicates that the Swiss financial center remains attractive for criminals and that the overall level of risks remains high.
The text is the third national risk assessment report on the subject. The diagnosis combines two elements: the national law enforcement system is overall solid, but must constantly adapt to new technologies used by offenders.
### Resources, sanctions and organized crime
To strengthen the Swiss response, the GCRF, the Interdepartmental Coordination Group responsible for combating money laundering, terrorist and proliferation financing, has made eight recommendations. Among the priorities is the strengthening of the staff of the authorities involved in fighting crime. The sharp increase in reports of suspected cases of money laundering risks pushing the control system to its limits.
The report therefore calls for additional staff for supervisory and enforcement authorities, more efficient IT systems and sufficient financial resources. A second chapter concerns financial supervision: the ongoing efforts to expand Finma's sanctioning arsenal must continue, with the aim of arriving at "effective and dissuasive sanctions".
The authors then point out the infiltration of organized crime into the legal economic fabric. Criminal networks use Switzerland to transfer funds and penetrate the legal economy; The GCRF requests that the ongoing bill against criminal organizations be submitted to Parliament as soon as possible.
Other recommendations include examining, and if necessary revising, the current Precious Metals Control Act. The GCRF also proposes to continuously monitor the transparency register relating to beneficial owner disclosures, in force since the beginning of October, to check whether it achieves its desired objectives. ## The practical reading of the report
The operational part of the dossier concerns first and foremost the system's ability to manage reports. The text links the massive increase in suspected money-laundering cases to the risk that the control system will reach its limits. The response indicated is not a single measure, but a combination of personnel, IT tools and financial resources for the supervisory and enforcement authorities.
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the point to follow is therefore the balance between the system's robustness and adaptation to the new tools used by criminals. The report does not present the system's resilience as a definitive result: it considers it sufficient overall, but subject to constant updating.
### Five fronts to distinguish
| Area | Signal in the report | Response indicated | | Controls | Massive growth in suspicious reports | More personnel, efficient IT and financial resources | | Supervision | Finma's sanctions arsenal to be expanded | Effective and deterrent sanctions | | Organized crime | Use of Switzerland for funds and infiltration into the legitimate economy | Prompt parliamentary review of the bill | | Precious metals | Need to examine the current law | Revision if appropriate | | Transparency | Register in force at the beginning of October | Constant evaluation of effects |
The table helps avoid confusing different levels. An increase in resources concerns administrative capacity; expanding sanctions concerns Finma's tools; the organized-crime bill concerns instead the passage to Parliament. These are paths linked by the report, but they do not coincide.
The transparency register also requires a cautious reading. The fact that it came into force at the beginning of October is not presented as automatic proof of the result: the GCRF recommends checking over time whether it produces the desired effects. The same applies to the law on precious metals, which the report calls for examining before any possible revision.
The message for the national debate is clear: the robustness recognized today does not eliminate the need to adapt controls, sanctions and regulatory instruments. The recommendations indicate precise directions, while their follow-up remains linked to the competent authorities and Parliament. ## How to follow the dossier without confusing proposals and decisions
The report offers a useful verification sequence for anyone who wants to follow the evolution of efforts to combat money laundering in Switzerland. The reading rule is to distinguish what is already stated in the document from the measures that the GCRF is calling for.
### Five verification steps
1. Start with the institutional status. The Federal Council has taken note of the report: this is the step recorded by the source. The eight recommendations, on the other hand, describe the interventions deemed necessary to improve the system. 2. Check operational capacity. The concrete reference is to the availability of personnel in the supervisory and enforcement authorities, the efficiency of IT systems, and the availability of sufficient financial resources. These are the three elements to look for when assessing the response to the massive increase in suspicious reports. 3. Keep financial supervision separate from the fight against organized crime. In the first case, the report discusses Finma’s sanctions arsenal and the objective of effective and dissuasive sanctions. In the second, it calls for the bill to be submitted to Parliament as soon as possible. 4. Follow the two areas of regulatory review. On the one hand, there is the current law on the control of precious metals, which is to be examined and, where appropriate, revised. On the other hand, there is the transparency register concerning beneficial owners, which came into force at the beginning of October: the question indicated by the report is whether it is producing the desired effects. 5. Keep the assessment separate from the outcomes. The source describes a system that is solid overall, but exposed to technological developments and the pressure of reports. Monitoring therefore does not end with taking note of the report: it concerns the implementation of the recommendations and the verification of the register’s effects.
This framework makes it possible to follow the issue at the federal level without attributing to Parliament decisions that the source does not report or treating measures presented as recommendations as already approved. ## TL;DR - The Federal Council launches the consultation on October 14, 2026 - Consultation deadline: January 28 - The proposal includes federal voting and signing initiatives and referendums - Geneva recognized the right in 2020
## Key facts - Initiator → Federal Council and some cantons - Subject → Constitutional amendment and amendment to the Political Rights Act - Recipients → Adult Swiss citizens - Rights indicated → National Council elections and federal votes - Other rights → Signing popular initiatives and referendums - Cantonal precedents → Geneva 2020; Appenzell Innerrhoden 2024
On October 14, 2026, the Federal Council launched the consultation procedure on the participation of people with intellectual disabilities in Switzerland’s political life. Like some cantons, it opened a process that will remain open until January 28. The dossier concerns a constitutional amendment and an amendment to the Political Rights Act.
The current framework at federal level provides for the exclusion of people with intellectual disabilities from exercising political rights, as a government note recalls. The proposal, by contrast, aims to enable adult Swiss citizens in the future to contribute to shaping the country’s policies, defining a federal-level framework different from today’s.
According to the objective outlined by the Federal Council, in the future all adult Swiss citizens should be able to participate in political life. The source concretely lists the forms of participation indicated: National Council elections, federal votes, the signing of popular initiatives and the signing of referendums. The list therefore includes both voting and signing the instruments specified.
### From the federal level to the cantons
The federal process runs alongside initiatives already mentioned in some cantons. In Geneva, in 2020, people with intellectual disabilities were granted the right to vote and stand for election at cantonal level; the text also cites Appenzell Innerrhoden in 2024. In other cantons, the source adds, similar efforts are under way. Institutionally, the Federal Council’s consultation is therefore presented alongside the cantonal processes already mentioned or still under way.
The report, broadcast in the 12.30 Radiogiornale on October 14, 2026, presents the prospect as a future one. The announced deadline for the consultation is January 28. The practical point to keep separate is the level at which the right is exercised. The source distinguishes the current federal situation, the consultation launched by the Federal Council, and the developments mentioned in some cantons. To read the news correctly, the cantonal recognition mentioned for Geneva should not be confused with the proposal concerning the Confederation.
| Level or territory | Source data | Scope | | --- | --- | --- | | Confederation | Currently excluded from federal political rights; consultation until January 28 | Perspective for adult Swiss citizens | | Geneva | Right to vote and to stand for election at cantonal level in 2020 | Cantonal level | | Appenzell Innerrhoden | Reference to 2024 | Cantonal level | | Other cantons | Similar efforts under way | Cantonal processes mentioned |
### What the federal perspective includes
The proposal described is not limited to a single election. The reference to elections to the National Council concerns participation in that federal vote; the reference to federal votes broadens the scope to the consultations indicated by the source. Signing popular initiatives and referendums adds the participation tools listed alongside voting.
The specified target group is precise: all adult Swiss citizens. For a practical reading, it is useful to associate the subject, level, and right: adult Swiss citizens, the Confederation, elections to the National Council, federal votes, popular initiatives or referendums.
The chronological comparison is equally useful. Geneva is placed in 2020, Appenzell Innerrhoden in 2024, while for the federal level the reference is October 14, 2026, with consultation until January 28. The other cantons are described as engaged in similar efforts. The overall picture therefore varies by territory and phase: some references concern the cantons, while others concern a federal consultation open until January 28. To follow the dossier without confusing the announcement, deadline and content, it is advisable to use a five-step checklist. The sequence remains faithful to the information provided and separates the federal level from the cantonal examples.
### The five references to note
1. **Start date.** Note October 14, 2026, the date of the report and the launch of the procedure by the Federal Council. 2. Deadline. Keep the January 28 deadline separate: it is the time limit indicated for the consultation. 3. Subject. Look for the two elements reported: a constitutional amendment and an amendment to the law on political rights. 4. Addressees and rights. Verify that the scope covers all adult Swiss citizens and includes the National Council, federal votes, popular initiatives and referendums. 5. Territorial comparison. Keep Geneva in 2020, Appenzell Innerrhoden in 2024 and the other cantons where similar efforts are under way separate.
This sequence helps prevent the consultation from being read as a federal right that has already been extended. The source in fact describes the current situation of exclusion at the federal level and presents extending participation as a future objective. The immediately usable time reference is therefore January 28, linked to the announced procedure.
Checking the institutional level also serves a practical purpose. If an update refers to the right to vote and stand for election in the context of Geneva, the reference is cantonal; if it mentions elections to the National Council, federal votes or signatures for initiatives and referendums, the scope is the one indicated for the federal proposal.

## Key facts
| Term | Value | |---|---| | Source | AutoScout24 | | Period | Third quarter | | New cars | -2,6% compared with the previous three months; -5,8% year on year | | Used cars | -0,8% compared with the second quarter; -4,3% year on year | | New petrol cars | -4,4% quarter on quarter; -4,9% year on year | | New plug-in hybrids | -16% year on year | | Used electric cars | +1,5% compared with April-June; -1,4% year on year | | Listings | +0,7% quarter on quarter; +2,6% year on year |
In the third quarter, in Switzerland, the average asking prices for new cars advertised on AutoScout24 fell by 2,6% compared with the previous quarter; year on year, the decline was 5,8%. The figure is reported in a market analysis published today by the portal, described as a leading player in the Confederation for vehicle sales. The news was reported by Keystone-ATS.
The decline also affected used cars: average prices were 0,8% lower than in the second quarter and 4,3% lower in the year-on-year comparison indicated by the analysis. The trend therefore concerns both main categories observed, with varying intensity.
### Categories with the largest changes
Among new cars, petrol vehicles fell by 4,4% compared with the previous quarter and by 4,9% compared with the previous year. The most substantial reduction concerned new plug-in hybrids: their cost fell by 16% year on year.
The picture for used electric cars is different over the short term. Prices rose by 1,5% compared with the April-June period, but the year-on-year comparison remains negative, with a decline of 1,4%. The source thus points to a difference between quarterly and annual trends, with no uniform development across powertrains.
As for supply, vehicle listings on AutoScout24 increased by 0,7% compared with the previous quarter and by 2,6% over a year. For used cars, the increase was 0,9% compared with the previous quarter and 2,5% year on year; listings for new cars, on the other hand, recorded a change of -0,8% in the quarterly comparison and +3,9% in the annual comparison.
The decline in prices is part of a trend that has already been observed for some time. In spring, AutoScout24, a platform belonging to Swiss Marketplace Group, or SMG, had reported the growing presence of Chinese manufacturers in Switzerland. Their offering combines lower costs, technological advances and a strong pace of innovation. According to the source, competition from Chinese brands is among the factors that could contribute to the decline in prices. To interpret the Swiss market picture without confusing different signals, it is useful to separate three questions: how much the average price changes, over what period the change is measured, and how many vehicles are advertised. AutoScout24's analysis places these elements within the same framework, but does not use them to describe the same dimension of the market.
### Price is not the only indicator
The quarterly and annual comparisons serve to show two distinct movements. The first highlights the most recent change, because it uses the previous three months as its reference; the second shows the trend compared with the annual period used by the analysis. For anyone examining a listing in Switzerland, this distinction prevents a short-term change from being treated as if it alone described the entire trend.
The number of listings also requires a separate reading. The total supply advertised on the platform has grown, while among new cars the quarterly figure fell and the annual figure rose. For used cars, on the other hand, both comparisons of listings indicate an increase. The resulting picture is complex: falling average prices and changing numbers of advertised vehicles are not the same data point.

Chinese competition adds another perspective. AutoScout24 had already reported the spread in Switzerland of more affordable manufacturers. The source, however, also links interest to technological progress and the speed of innovation. The phenomenon is therefore not presented solely as a price war: the offerings of Chinese brands are described in terms of cost, technology and innovation.
For a national reader, the practical point is to keep these three checks separate when consulting the platform's data. First, identify the vehicle category, then look at the comparison period, and finally consider the evolution of listings. Only in this way can the reduction in price quotations be read together with, but not confused with, the evolution of supply. ### A simple procedure for reading a listing
Anyone considering a vehicle in Switzerland can use the update as a checklist, without turning the platform's average figure into an individual decision. The first step is to choose the scope: a new car or a used vehicle. The source in fact shows two markets with distinct changes, so mixing them in the same comparison makes the reading less clear.

### Five-step check
1. Select the vehicle category and keep new and used vehicles separate. 2. Note the type of powertrain, distinguishing petrol, plug-in hybrid and used electric vehicles. 3. Read the quarterly and annual figures as different comparisons. 4. Check the number of listings relating to the selected category. 5. Consider competition from Chinese brands alongside costs, technology and innovation.
The third step is particularly useful for powertrains that show misaligned signals. The source in fact describes a quarterly trend different from the annual one for used electric vehicles. Applying the same check to the other categories helps avoid focusing only on the most recent figure.
The fourth step serves to place the listing within the offering observed on AutoScout24. The total number of vehicles and the number of new or used listings do not necessarily move in the same way; for this reason, it is advisable to look at the entry corresponding to the vehicle being examined, rather than replacing it with the total.
Finally, Chinese competition should be recorded as one element of the overall picture, not as the sole explanation.
