item.title: Corporate bankruptcies sharply on the rise, record high in 2025-2026
item.description: 11’063 insolvent companies between January and September Company bankruptcies at 13’660, +38,4% year-on-year New registrations in the register: 41’706 Individuals: 8’003 bankruptcies
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 11’063 insolvent companies between January and September - Company bankruptcies at 13’660, +38,4% year-on-year - New registrations in the register: 41’706 - Individuals: 8’003 bankruptcies in the first nine months
## Key facts - Period → January–September - Corporate insolvencies → 11’063 (+45,6%) - Organizational deficiencies → 2’597 (+14,2%) - Total company bankruptcies → 13’660 (+38,4%) - New registrations → 41’706 (+2,1%) - Deletions → 26’712 (+4,9%) - Private bankruptcies → 8’003 (+6,3%) - Expected company closures in 2026 → over 19’000
Between January and September, 11’063 companies in Switzerland filed for insolvency, as they were unable to meet their payment obligations. The figure, released by the economic information company Creditreform and reported by Keystone-ATS, is 45,6% higher than in the same period of 2025. The survey covers Switzerland.
In addition to insolvency proceedings, there were 2’597 closures due to organizational deficiencies, as provided for under Article 731b of the Code of Obligations. This category increased by 14,2%. The total number of company bankruptcies thus reached 13’660 cases, an annual increase of 38,4%.
Also contributing was the legislative amendment that entered into force at the beginning of 2025. Since then, public-law institutions have been required to collect arrears from companies through bankruptcy proceedings. They were thus placed on an equal footing with private creditors. Creditreform experts argue that the former privilege led companies to fulfill their obligations to public creditors insufficiently.
> “The abolition of this privilege had been long awaited.”
Creditreform also links the increase in bankruptcies to the boom in new companies, which has been underway for several years. The company notes that young businesses are particularly exposed to the risk of closure during their first five years of operation.
### New registrations and cancellations
During the period under review, there were 41’706 new registrations in the commercial register, an increase of 2,1%. Deletions reached 26’712, an increase of 4,9%, resulting in a net increase of 14’994 companies. Creditreform estimates that new companies could reach 57’000 over the course of 2026, a record level.
Among private individuals, there were 8’003 bankruptcies, an increase of 6,3%. Renounced inheritances, at 6’353, increased by 3,8%; bankruptcies of living persons rose by 17,2% to 1’650, but were still fewer in absolute terms. ## A practical reading of the picture
For those following the Swiss economy, the most useful figure is not a single number, but the way Creditreform separates the causes. The total for companies includes insolvencies, linked to the inability to meet payments, and closures due to organizational shortcomings. Reading only the total therefore risks concealing two different mechanisms. The correct comparison is between the same item and the same period, not between aggregates constructed differently.
### A market that opens and closes in the same period
The snapshot of businesses also shows a double movement. Entries in the commercial register are increasing, but so are removals. The net growth of 14’994 companies does not erase the fact that 26’712 were removed during the period: it describes a positive balance between two distinct movements, not the absence of closures. Creditreform specifically identifies the boom in new businesses as a possible component of the increase in bankruptcies and points to the first five years as a particularly vulnerable phase for young companies.
There is also the effect of the regulations in force since the beginning of 2025. Public-law institutions have been placed on an equal footing with private creditors when requesting payment of overdue claims through bankruptcy proceedings. To interpret the year-on-year increase, this change should be kept separate from the other factors cited by the company: the figure is also influenced by the change in the procedures initiated.
### Estimate, not actual figure
The estimate of more than 19’000 business closures for 2026 should be read as a Creditreform forecast, not as a figure already recorded. For individuals, the annual estimate is more than 10’600 bankruptcies. The comparison with the approximately 8’000 bankruptcies in 2019, the last pre-Covid year cited by the source, serves to measure the historical gap.
For individuals, however, the picture has a different composition: rejected inheritances account for the majority, while the bankruptcies of living people have a smaller absolute weight, despite increasing sharply. Distinguishing these categories prevents the same dynamic from being attributed to households and companies. ## From the news to an orderly verification
To use the information operationally, the most prudent approach is a sequence of checks that separates categories, periods and forecasts. For those who manage a business, have dealings with a company or follow Swiss data, there are five steps:
1. Start with the period: January–September is the window used for the observed data. Do not overlap it with the forecast for all of 2026, which concerns a different time span.
2. Isolate the cause: the inability to meet payments corresponds to insolvencies; organizational deficiencies are the category referred to by Article 731b of the Code of Obligations.
3. Since the beginning of 2025, public-law institutions must require companies to pay arrears through bankruptcy proceedings, just like private creditors.
4. Separate private individuals: rejected inheritances and bankruptcies of living persons are counted separately. Maintaining this division avoids reading 8’003 cases as a single phenomenon.
5. Treat projections as such: the more than 19’000 business closures expected for 2026 are an estimate by Creditreform. For historical comparison, use the approximately 8’000 bankruptcies in 2019 indicated by the source.
### What to monitor over time
The first element to monitor is the transition from the data for the first nine months to the close of all of 2026. Creditreform indicates an expected threshold, not a final tally; verification will therefore have to compare the forecast with the final number of business closures. The same criterion applies to net growth: the balance between registrations and deletions describes the overall movement, but does not replace a separate reading of the two series.
The distinction between proceedings also serves to avoid automatically attributing every increase to the same cause. Insolvency concerns the inability to meet payments; organizational deficiencies are a different category, referred to by Article 731b of the Code of Obligations. For public creditors, the date to bear in mind is the beginning of 2025, when the amendment equating them with private creditors in proceedings for arrears claims entered into force.
Those who want to turn a reading of the business landscape into a search for employers can consult aziende che assumono.
*Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/fallimenti-in-netto-aumento%2c-%c3%a8-record-per-quelli-aziendali/92213801)*

item.title: Pension funds: illiquid investments account for 36% of assets
item.description: 36% of the assets are in investments that are not immediately tradable The share has grown over the past 15 years Real estate, mortgages and alternative investments offer stability
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 36% of the assets is held in investments that cannot be traded immediately - The share has increased over the past 15 years - Real estate, mortgages and alternative investments offer stability, but less flexibility - Risks emerge when multiple stress factors occur together
## Key facts - Location → Zurich - Study → Complementa's 2026 Risk Check-up - Share → approximately 36% of assets - Period → past 15 years - Assets → real estate, alternative investments and mortgages - Risk → delayed sale or sale at price discounts in the event of turbulence
ZURICH – In Swiss pension fund portfolios, so-called illiquid investments are taking up an increasingly large share. With low interest rates, the search for new sources of returns has caused the share of funds allocated to these assets to rise significantly.
According to experts, diversification is not in itself a bad idea. The trade-off, however, is a less flexible portfolio: real estate, mortgages and alternative investments cannot be traded as quickly as shares. If a fund has to sell at short notice, the transaction may become more difficult.
### The 2026 Risk Check-up finding
The picture emerges from Complementa's 2026 Risk Check-up. The study indicates that, over the past 15 years, the share of illiquid investments held by Swiss pension funds has increased significantly. Taking real estate, alternative investments and mortgages into account, approximately 36% of assets are now invested in assets that cannot be traded immediately.
The sought-after advantage is stable returns. The source associates this choice with the search for new sources of returns during a period of low interest rates. But the same structure makes a sale more complex, especially if the real estate market were to cool sharply or if the debt of some countries were to become a problem.
### The moment of stress
For experts, the situation remains manageable as long as markets remain stable and the funds have sufficient liquidity. Difficulties arise when several stress factors occur simultaneously. Among the possible scenarios, Complementa includes severe market turbulence, during which institutions may need liquidity in the short term to meet their obligations or adjust the structure of their portfolios.
Some funds are already preparing by focusing primarily on further investments in Swiss real estate and infrastructure, with the aim of limiting geopolitical risks. If markets enter a phase of severe turbulence, however, illiquid investments can only be sold after a delay or at considerable discounts. Moreover, compared with securities listed on the stock exchange, their valuation and the measurement of returns are more complex.
In private equity and private debt, investors' capital commitments may extend over several years, while both the timing and the magnitude of returns remain uncertain. Complementa therefore emphasizes the importance of identifying liquidity needs at an early stage and maintaining adequate reserves. ### Three scenarios to distinguish
The practical interpretation of the figure starts with a simple distinction: return and liquidity are not the same thing. A property, a mortgage or an alternative investment can contribute to stable returns, but it does not offer the same flexibility as a stock when the fund needs to raise cash quickly. The 36% indicated by Complementa therefore also measures the portfolio's room for manoeuvre.
| Situation | Effect on illiquid investments | |---|---| | Stable markets and sufficient liquidity | The trend does not pose a problem | | Turbulence and short-term liquidity needs | Delayed sale or sale at a discount | | Portfolio reorientation | More complex valuations and performance measurement |
The risk is not triggered by every market fluctuation. According to experts, it becomes critical when several stress factors coincide: the fund must meet obligations or reorient the portfolio, while a significant portion of its assets is not immediately tradable. At that point, the difference compared with listed securities concerns both the time needed to sell and the price that can be obtained.
### Why real estate matters
Specialists identify a point of vulnerability in real estate, which accounts for more than a fifth of pension funds' assets. If the sector loses momentum or faces a prolonged correction in prices and demand, sales may become more difficult and valuations may come under pressure. For a fund, the problem is not only the theoretical value of the asset: the possibility of converting it into liquidity when needed also matters.
Private equity and private debt add a different kind of rigidity. Investors often have to honor capital commitments over several years, but they do not know with certainty the timing and amount of return flows. This can limit the ability to quickly adapt the portfolio to changed market or liquidity conditions. In a crisis, a sudden shortage of liquidity can therefore turn an investment intended for the long term into a disadvantage.
For now, the financial situation eases the pressure: the majority of Swiss pension funds have a comfortable funding ratio, in some cases at record levels, and benefit from high returns. This financial strength supports increased investment in infrastructure, real estate and other alternative assets, but does not eliminate the risk associated with several stress factors occurring at the same time. ### A five-step operational framework
To follow the topic, the practical approach can start with the criteria used by Complementa. Returns and liquidity should be considered separately, together with the portfolio's response to stress.
1. Separate the categories. Distinguish real estate, mortgages and alternative investments: these are the components included in the 36% of assets that are not immediately tradable. 2. Measure the real estate weighting. Real estate accounts for more than one fifth of wealth. Prices and demand should be monitored because a prolonged correction can make sales more difficult and depress valuations. 3. Check commitments. In private equity and private debt, capital may be tied up for several years; the timing and amount of returns remain uncertain. 4. Simulate stress. Examine together severe market turbulence, the need for short-term liquidity and the need to honour commitments or reorient the portfolio. 5. Check reserves. With more assets tied up for the long term, it becomes crucial to identify liquidity needs in good time and maintain sufficient reserves.
### The criterion for assessing choices
To limit geopolitical risks, some pension funds intend to allocate additional resources to Swiss real estate and infrastructure. This approach does not, however, guarantee liquidity: during turbulence, a sale may still require time or a discount on the price.
The comparison should also be made with listed securities: for illiquid assets, valuation and performance measurement are more complex. If the portfolio needs to be reoriented quickly, this complexity is added to the time required for a sale.
> “As the amount of assets tied up for the long term increases, it becomes increasingly essential for a pension fund to identify liquidity needs promptly and maintain adequate reserves”.
For those following Swiss pension provision, the useful check is threefold: the non-tradable share, future commitments and available reserves. These are the three elements that link the aggregate percentage to the portfolio's actual flexibility.
To learn more about pension provision, consult guida alla pensione.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/economia/1956672/investimenti-casse-pensioni-illiquidi-rischi)*

On August 28, 2026, a violent thunderstorm hit Switzerland with strong gusts of wind and hail. In some locations, the hailstones reached a diameter of up to five centimeters. The cantons identified as the hardest hit are Bern, Solothurn, Aargau, Zurich and Thurgau.

### The geographical scale of the damage
The relatively high population density of the affected area contributed to the scale of the estimated losses, Camara explained. The Swiss Re executive also outlined a worst-case scenario, noting that the same event in Zurich would probably have caused an even greater loss.
The figure distinguishes total insured damage from the motor vehicle component. The first figure describes the event as a whole; the second shows the weight of automobiles in the estimate. The prevention measures indicated by the group include warnings issued as promptly as possible and access to covered parking.

## TL;DR - Guy Parmelin to leave the Federal Council on 31.12.2026 - AHV/IV pensions will increase by around 1.6% - The Swiss-EU package has been in parliament since 13 March 2026 - The popular vote is scheduled for November 29, 2026
## Key facts - Resignation: 31.12.2026 - AVS/AI adjustment: starting from January, approximately 1.6% - Commitment credit: up to 10 billion - Switzerland-EU package: 13 March 2026 - Popular vote: 29 November 2026
Guy Parmelin will leave the Federal Council on 31.12.2026. The President of the Confederation has announced his resignation and Parliament will elect his successor during the next session. The statement is referred to as a press conference.
The overview brings together different levels of federal activity: the resignation announced by Guy Parmelin, the pension update, the financial stabilization credit, the cybersecurity proposal, the Switzerland-EU package and the popular vote. The text thus combines decisions, projects and institutional appointments.
The official portal of the Swiss Government offers updated information on the decisions and activities of the Federal Council, on its functioning as a collegial body and on popular votes.
### Pension and finance
From January, AVS/AI pensions will grow by approximately 1.6%, in line with the trend in prices and wages. At the same time, the maximum amount payable into the third pillar will also increase. To follow the topic of annuities, guida alle rendite AVS is available.
The Government wants to renew the commitment credit which would allow Switzerland to provide up to 10 billion in the event of a crisis. The indicated objective is to allow the country to continue contributing to the stabilization of the global financial system.
### Cybersecurity and relations with the EU
The Federal Council also intends to strengthen cybersecurity with a law dedicated to software and hardware products, data and digital infrastructures. A proposal will be drawn up by June 2027: the source then sets a deadline for its preparation.
Switzerland and the EU have negotiated a new package of agreements to stabilize and develop bilateral relations. The Federal Council forwarded it to Parliament on 13 March 2026.
The democratic calendar finally indicates November 29, 2026. On that date, Swiss citizens will express their opinion on the additional financing of the AVS, on the fireworks initiative, on the taxation of spouses and on the law on war material. ## How to read practical effects
Decisions have different times and recipients. For those receiving an AVS/AI annuity, the operational reference is the start in January and the adjustment linked to prices and wages. For those who use the third pillar, the data to follow is the new maximum limit allowed. The source presents the two changes in the same update, but they remain two different pension planning items. To learn more about the second aspect, consult guida al terzo pilastro.
| Dossier | Indicated horizon | Effect described | |---|---|---| | AVS/AI pensions | Starting January | Adjustment of approximately 1.6% to the evolution of prices and wages | | Third pillar | In the same update | Increase in maximum allowable deposit | | Commitment credit | In case of crisis | Up to 10 billion for the stabilization of the global financial system | | Cybersecurity | By June 2027 | Proposal on software, hardware, data and digital infrastructures | | Switzerland-EU | March 13, 2026 | Package sent to Parliament | | Popular vote | November 29, 2026 | Four objects subjected to Swiss citizens |
### Decisions already scheduled and dossiers in evolution
The table distinguishes an effect with an indicated starting date, such as the adjustment of pensions, from a credit in the event of a crisis, from a proposal to be developed and from a package already sent to Parliament. The commitment credit is linked to a crisis situation and Switzerland's ability to contribute to global financial stabilization. Annuities and the third pillar are described in the social security part.
Cybersecurity is also presented as a legislative path with a proposal expected by June 2027. The indicated perimeter includes software and hardware products, data and digital infrastructures. For the reader, the dossier should be followed as a regulatory development distinct from the social security adjustment placed in January.
The Switzerland-EU package, however, was transmitted to Parliament on 13 March 2026. The declared aim is to stabilize and develop bilateral relations. November 29, 2026 belongs to another channel: the popular vote, with four distinct objects. Separating these paths helps to avoid treating a social security measure, a bill, a package of agreements and a citizens' consultation as equivalent.

To turn decisions into a practical reminder, it is best to separate five steps and assign each its own date or condition.
1. Starting from January, check the adaptation of AVS/AI pensions to the evolution of prices and wages. The indicated increase is approximately 1.6%. 2. In the same period, check the new maximum payment allowed into the third pillar. The point to note is the expected limit increase. 3. For the succession to the Federal Council, mark 31.12.2026: Guy Parmelin has announced his resignation and Parliament will elect his successor during the next session. 4. For institutional dossiers, keep separate the Switzerland-EU package, transmitted to Parliament on 13 March 2026, and the proposal on cybersecurity, to be drawn up by June 2027. 5. If you are a Swiss citizen, note down November 29, 2026 to vote on the four listed items: AVS supplementary financing, Fireworks initiative, Spouse tax and War material law.
### A reminder not to confuse deadlines
This order puts the operational dates first and then the political steps. January concerns annuities and the third pillar; the next session concerns the election of the successor; March 13, 2026 identifies the transmission of the Switzerland-EU package; June 2027 concerns the development of the cybersecurity proposal; November 2026 is about the popular vote.
The commitment credit follows a different logic: the Government wants to renew it to allow Switzerland to provide up to 10 billion in the event of a crisis. It should therefore be kept in the dossier of the stabilization of the global financial system, not in the annuity calendar.
For those who are organizing their budget, the starting point remains to distinguish the AVS/AI pension from the maximum payment of the third pillar. For those who follow federal politics, however, it is better to keep Parliament, Government and citizens separate: the former will elect the successor, the latter has indicated the projects and the citizens will vote on the objects of November 29th.

item.title: Wage gap among young people in Switzerland: income gap narrows
item.description: Among those born in 1995, the income gap is 14% Among those born in 1965, the gap was 55% In 2025, 54% of young women have a tertiary qualification
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Among those born in 1995, the income gap is 14% - Among those born in 1965, the gap was 55% - In 2025, 54% of young women held a tertiary qualification - Among parents, the gap remains at 51%
## Key facts - Study → University of Lausanne and Swiss Foundation for Social Science Research fors - Researchers → Daniel Oesch and Oliver Lipps - Sample → over 215,000 people between the ages of 25 and 34 - Data period → 1991-2024 - Tertiary education in 2025 → 54% of young women and 48% of young men
In the 25-34 age group, women born in 1995 had an overall working income 14% lower than men. The data emerges from a study conducted by the University of Lausanne and the Swiss Foundation for Social Science Research Fors, published in the journal "Social Change in Switzerland".
Daniel Oesch and Oliver Lipps analysed data on over 215,000 people aged 25-34 from Swiss workforce surveys conducted from 1991 to 2024. In the statement related to the study, the two researchers define evolution as a "race to recovery".
### Comparison between generations
Among people aged 25-34 born in 1965, women's overall work income was 55% lower than that of men. In the 1995 cohort, the difference had narrowed to 14%. The comparison then signals a sharp downsizing, but the gap remains.
Other indicators also show the rapprochement between the sexes. The difference in the weekly schedule has been reduced from 17 hours to less than four hours. The difference in standardized hourly pay has grown from nearly 20% to less than 5%. Participation in the labor market has also approached between the two sexes, according to the results of the study.
Among the decisive elements, the study identifies the change in trend at the educational level. In 2025, in Switzerland, 54% of young women had obtained a tertiary degree, compared to 48% of young men. The category includes universities, vocational university schools and higher vocational education. The research also indicates an advancement of women towards professions with higher salary potential.
Motherhood continues to make an important difference: after the formation of a family, the income distance increases significantly. For women without children, the gap narrowed from 27% to 7%; among parents it also fell, but remained much wider, at 51%. The distinction between total income and hourly pay is also useful to read your data in calcolatore stipendio. The practical significance of the study emerges when one avoids treating 14% as the only useful figure. Overall labor income, weekly hours and standardized hourly pay describe different dimensions of the gap. Bringing them together allows for a more precise reading of the improvement recorded between generations.
### Three measures not to confuse
| Indicator | Born in 1965 | Born in 1995 | |---|---:|---:| | Overall labor income | 55% | 14% | | Difference in weekly hours | 17 hours | less than four hours | | Standardized hourly pay | nearly 20% | less than 5% |
Overall income is the measure with which the study describes the shift from 55% to 14%. Weekly hours instead measure the difference in time worked: from 17 hours to less than four. Standardized hourly pay follows another scale, from nearly 20% to less than 5%. The three results are not interchangeable.
For those monitoring their own busta paga svizzera, the practical consequence is to separate hourly pay from overall labor income and not use a single figure to describe the entire position.
The educational advantage adds another element. In 2025, 54% of young women had a tertiary qualification, compared with 48% of young men, and women were moving toward professions with higher salary potential. The study presents this reversal as one of the key factors behind the catch-up, not as the automatic elimination of the gap.
The difference between 7% for women without children and 51% among parents then makes it necessary to distinguish family trajectories. The 7% cannot be read as a result that applies to all women, because the source reports a markedly wider gap after family formation.
The international comparison completes the picture: for those born in 1965, Switzerland had the second-largest gap compared with France, Sweden, Great Britain and the United States; for those born in 1995, it had the smallest. Progress can therefore also be measured against other countries, even though a gap remains.

To apply the study to a personal salary comparison, it is useful to follow a sequence of four checks. The aim is not to turn a collective statistic into a definitive assessment, but to use the same indicators to examine one’s own case more precisely.
### Four checks for interpreting your own data
- First: distinguish total employment income from standardized hourly pay. These are the two income measures used in the study and should not be merged into a single item. - Second: note the difference in weekly hours. The study’s comparison goes from 17 hours to less than four hours; this parameter should be kept separate from the total amount. - Third: consider the family situation. The reference changes between women without children, for whom the difference fell from 27% to 7%, and parents, among whom it remains at 51%. - Fourth: consider education and occupation together. In 2025, tertiary education applied to 54% of young women and 48% of young men; the study links this reversal to occupations with higher salary potential.
For anyone evaluating a job, a comparison with annunci di lavoro should be made while maintaining the same unit of measurement: total income, weekly hours or standardized hourly pay. Mixing these levels makes it difficult to understand which difference is being observed.
The scope of the data should be preserved. The analysis concerns people between 25 and 34 years old and uses Swiss labor force surveys conducted from 1991 to 2024. The percentages therefore describe a trend across generations, not a figure to be applied indiscriminately to every worker.
The family comparison also requires attention: the source separates women without children and parents, while the advantage in education and women’s advancement toward occupations with higher salary potential are described as factors in the overall evolution. Keeping these elements separate avoids attributing the entire gap to a single cause.
This process makes it possible to check one’s comparison without losing sight of the meaning of the data: first define the measure, then consider the hours, then the family context and finally the relationship with education and occupation. item.description: The Federal Administration offers meaningful work Recent graduates have a wide range of internships 50 training programs are available

## TL;DR - The Federal Administration offers meaningful work - Recent graduates have a wide range of internships - 50 vocational training programs are available - Trainees have 7 weeks of vacation
## Key facts - Employer → Federal Administration - Internships → wide range for recent graduates - Vocational training → 50 - Holidays → 7 weeks - Employee offering → flexible forms of work, performance-based remuneration and continuing education
### The offering at the center The Federal Administration presents work within its structures as an activity with a tangible impact on Switzerland: the talent, ideas and commitment of those who work there contribute to the country’s high quality of life. The offering therefore invites people to view employment also as a contribution to the smooth functioning of Switzerland.
At the Federal Administration, work is described as meaningful. Those who perform it can assume responsibility, work for the well-being of the population in Switzerland and develop innovative solutions within multidisciplinary teams. The teamwork dimension is part of the proposition for those who want to put their talent and ideas to good use.
For recent graduates, the Federal Administration offers a wide range of internships. The experience makes it possible to gain valuable practical experience, expand one’s network of contacts and use one’s knowledge to help shape Switzerland’s future. The internship is thus presented as a concrete experience, linked both to learning and to personal contribution.
Alongside internships, there is vocational training. The offering comprises 50 vocational training programs: those who choose one work on concrete tasks and projects, learn with the support of their trainers and acquire skills for their future. There are also 7 weeks of holidays, with time to devote to relaxation, hobbies, travel and friends.
The declared common thread is contributing to Switzerland’s future. In work at the Federal Administration, this happens through responsibility and innovative solutions; in internships, through practical experience, networking and knowledge; in training, through real tasks, guidance and skills.
Finally, the Federal Administration presents its offering as an employer with flexible working arrangements, performance-based remuneration, continuing education opportunities and additional proposals. Those who wish to broaden the comparison can set this offering alongside annunci di lavoro, without losing sight of the three paths indicated by the source. ### How to read the three opportunities The practical value of the proposal becomes clear when the three paths are separated, because each option addresses a different need. The question to ask is simple: are you looking for meaningful work, experience after your studies, or vocational training? The answer guides the reading of the characteristics indicated by the source.
| Path | Elements to assess | | Work in the Federal Administration | responsibility, population well-being, innovative solutions and multidisciplinary teams | | Internship | hands-on experience, network of contacts and knowledge | | Vocational training | 50 pathways, real tasks and projects, trainers, skills and 7 weeks of vacation |
For a recent graduate, the internship is presented primarily as a step toward gaining experience. It is not only about learning: the network of contacts and the use of one's knowledge are part of the same path. Its distinctive feature, according to the source, is the relationship between what one already knows and what one can experience in the field. The proposal thus combines experience with contributing to Switzerland's future.
Those seeking vocational training, on the other hand, find a broader offering, organized into 50 options. The presence of real tasks and projects makes the practical component concrete; the support provided by trainers indicates the role of guidance; skills development is forward-looking. The 7 weeks of vacation add to the training a period explicitly intended for relaxation, hobbies, travel and friends.
For those considering the Federal Administration as an employer, the point of comparison is different. Flexible working arrangements, performance-based remuneration and continuing education make up the overall offering. They should not be confused with internships or the 50 training programs: they describe how the Administration presents itself as an employer. Those who want to broaden the comparison can also look at the aziende che assumono, keeping the path, objective and offering separate.

1. Start from your starting point. If you are a recent graduate, focus on the wide range of internships. If you are looking for training, explore the 50 professional options. If you are considering an employer, instead look at flexible forms of work, performance-based pay and continuing education.
2. Define the result you want to achieve. For an internship, the reference points are hands-on experience, networking and applying knowledge. For vocational training, the focus should be on real tasks and projects, support from trainers and skills development. For work at the Federal Administration, the text highlights responsibility, the well-being of the population and innovative solutions in multidisciplinary teams.
3. Check what place everyday life occupies. In the vocational training path, the 7 weeks of vacation are associated with relaxation, hobbies, travel and friends. This element should be considered together with work on real projects and learning from the trainers, not as a separate detail.

The annunci di lavoro help broaden your perspective, while the Federal Administration page makes it possible to identify the vocational training that is right for you. ## TL;DR - The Graubünden Government appoints Müller to the BCG Bank Council - Term: July 1, 2027 - June 30, 2031 - Caviezel leaves after three terms due to the term limit - Sutter-Rüdisser: another four years and the vice presidency
## Key facts - Decision → Rhaetian Government - New member → Reto Müller - Taking office → July 1, 2027 - End of term → June 30, 2031 - Vice President → Michèle F. Sutter-Rüdisser
The Rhaetian Government has chosen Reto Müller for a seat on the Bank Council of Banca cantonale grigione (BCG). With the same decision, Michèle F. Sutter-Rüdisser’s term as a member of the Bank Council was extended by another four years, and she was designated vice president of the body. These are decisions concerning the institution’s highest governing body, announced in a communication from the executive.
For the reader following banche in Svizzera, the central point is the future composition of the Bank Council. The note focuses on the body’s composition and does not address products, services or customer terms. The timetable is already specified precisely, although the changeover is not immediate.
### The succession and the dates
Müller will take office on July 1, 2027, and will remain in the position until June 30, 2031. After three terms of office, Christoph Caviezel will leave the position because of the limit set for the duration of the term. The text therefore distinguishes the appointment from the actual start of the term.
The Government expresses its gratitude to Caviezel for his long, valuable and fruitful service as a member and vice president of the Bank Council. In the text, his departure is attributed to the limit set for the duration of the term, not to any other reason.
### The profiles set out in the note
Müller’s profile includes many years of experience in the financial sector. He held various managerial positions at Credit Suisse and UBS for more than thirty years. The text does not attribute to him any position other than that of a member of the Bank Council.
Since 2021, Sutter-Rüdisser has been a member of the Bank Council. At the School of Management of the University of St. Gallen, she is a professor of economics and also serves on several boards of directors. The extension of her term and her appointment as vice president renew and broaden her position on the same body. The practical significance of the decision lies in the distinction between continuity and succession. On the one hand, the body retains Sutter-Rüdisser, who has served on it since 2021 and is designated vice president. On the other, it indicates Müller's future entry within a defined time window and Caviezel's departure after three terms. The source allows the changeover to be read as a planned transition, without turning it into an immediate change for those looking at BCG from the outside.
### Before and after, according to the note
| Aspect | Situation indicated | Transition | |---|---|---| | Composition | Caviezel leaves the position | Müller will join as a member | | Vice presidency | Caviezel is also identified as the outgoing vice president | Sutter-Rüdisser is designated vice president | | Duration | Three terms for Caviezel | Müller: from July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2031 |
The table clarifies a point that should not be confused: Müller's appointment concerns the Bank Council, while the vice presidency is assigned to Sutter-Rüdisser. The text does not say that Müller will assume the vice presidency.
### What can and cannot be inferred
For those who use or observe a cantonal bank, the announcement primarily provides information about those responsible for the supreme body. It does not communicate changes to products or customer terms. For this reason, it does not allow one to state that the institution's day-to-day activities will change.
The comparison of the profiles in the note highlights different areas of expertise: Müller held management positions at Credit Suisse and UBS for more than thirty years, while Sutter-Rüdisser is an economics lecturer at the School of Management of the University of St. Gallen and serves on several boards of directors. For those looking for tools in the sector, the conti bancari in Svizzera are also available, but this service information should be kept separate from the announced appointment.

To follow the changeover without attributing to the notice effects it does not contain, the reader can use a simple framework. There is no need to turn the appointment into a prediction about BCG's services: the position, date and profile should be kept separate.
### The checklist for reading the appointment
1. Identify the body. The decision concerns the Bank Council, defined in the source as BCG's supreme body. This is the level at which the news should be understood.
2. Separate appointment and taking office. Reto Müller has been appointed, but will take office on July 1, 2027, and the stated term ends on June 30, 2031. The date prevents presenting the change as already completed.
3. Verify the replacement. The name linked to the departure is Christoph Caviezel, who is leaving after three terms because of the term limit. The Government thanks him for his work, including as vice president.
4. Distinguish the offices. Sutter-Rüdisser is not presented as Müller's replacement: her term is extended for another four years and she is designated vice president. The source states that she has been a member since 2021.
These four steps make it possible to correctly read any future updates to the same matter: it will be possible to check whether they concern the composition of the Council, the dates already indicated, or internal roles. ## Key facts - Bodies National → Council, Council of States and Federal Plenary Assembly - → Search Advanced Search, Curia Vista and Official Bulletin - → EFTA/EU relations, NATO PA and OECD DP - Memory → Deputies since 1848, presidents and legislatures
The page of the Swiss Parliament opens with a broad structure, but the first level is clear: National Council, Council of States and Plenary Federal Assembly. For the two Chambers, the sections of the Office, the President, the members A–Z, the members per Canton, the arrangement of the seats and the mutations are indicated. MEPs from 1848 and advanced research also appear for the Plenary Assembly.
### Rooms, committees and delegations
This organization distinguishes people, organs and acts. The portal separates thematic committees, supervisory committees, special committees and other committees. The menu lists CPE, CAG, CSSS, CAPTE, CTT, CET, CSEC, CPS, and CIP, along with reports, consultation items, subcommittees, and working groups. There are also attributions, reference documents and links.
An autonomous part is dedicated to delegations and international parliamentary relations. The portal features EFTA/EU, DCE, NATO AP, OSCE AP, OECD DP and the Permanent Delegations for Relations with Parliaments of Neighbouring States. Thislast area includes the Bundestag, the French Parliament, the Italian Parliament, the Landtag of Liechtenstein and the Austrian Parliament, with entries dedicated to activities, calendars and legal bases.

The available material does not present a single decision involving amounts, deadlines or a specific regulatory change. Instead, it presents a framework for reconstructing the activity of the Federal Assembly: the question is linked to the relevant item, vote, session, committee or archive. For a national reader, this distinction helps them immediately choose the correct section.

The first path starts with Curia Vista when looking for an item or a response to a parliamentary intervention. Advanced search is used to narrow the search; the Curia Vista explained page instead provides guidance on the tool. If the interest concerns the outcome of a vote, the National Council voting database and the xls file represent a separate step. The Official Bulletin adds the explanations dedicated to the document.
For finances, the menu places on an equal footing the Budget procedure, financial management tools, types of credit and spending limit, supplementary credits and the Budget with integrated task and financial plan, also referred to as PICF. item.title: Hackers send refrigerators haywire: “It could happen in Switzerland too”
item.description: Attack on around 150 supermarkets in France Refrigerators up to 50 degrees and tons of food thrown away Danfoss: vulnerabilities in Internet-connected systems
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Attack on approximately 150 supermarkets in France - Refrigerators reaching up to 50 degrees and tons of food thrown away - Danfoss: vulnerability in systems connected to the Internet - For the HSLU expert, the risk also exists in Switzerland
## Key facts - What → cyberattack on refrigerated display cases - When → overnight Sunday to Monday - Where → around 150 supermarkets in France - Temperatures → up to 50 degrees - Manufacturer → Danfoss - Manipulated function → defrosting - Expert → Sebastian Obermeier, HSLU - Update → distributed in 2025
Overnight from Sunday to Monday, a cyberattack hit around 150 supermarkets in France, including branches of Intermarché, Netto and Carrefour. The hackers remotely manipulated the refrigeration systems: the refrigerators went out of control, with temperatures reaching up to 50 degrees and tonnes of food having to be discarded. The incident also raised a question for Swiss large-scale retailers: could a similar attack hit Migros, Coop, Aldi or Lidl?
### Access to the refrigeration systems
Sebastian Obermeier, a cybersecurity expert at the Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts, believes the risk exists. The attackers are believed to have exploited vulnerabilities in Danfoss systems connected to the internet, interfering with the defrosting function. The expert told 20 Minuten that initial access was less complex because the systems were accessible online and apparently had known vulnerabilities. Changing the parameters, however, requires specific expertise. item.description: FAR: approximately 20'000 beneficiaries notified after an attack Publica: approximately 112'000 people potentially involved A software provider can expose

## TL;DR - FAR: approximately 20'000 beneficiaries notified after an attack - Publica: approximately 112'000 people potentially involved - A software provider can expose multiple pension funds in a single blow - The scam used the French prefix 0033
## Key facts - Fondazione FAR → approximately 20'000 beneficiaries - Publica → approximately 112'000 people potentially affected - PK Softech → Reinach (BL), active for over twenty years - Canton Bern pension funds → over 92'000 insured persons - Post Office pension fund → 67'000 insured persons - Migros pension fund → 75'500 insured persons - Call prefix → 0033
### The phone call that triggered the alarm
A pensioner from central Switzerland was called by a female voice for two days in a row. She spoke impeccable Swiss German, but the number displayed the French prefix 0033.
The pensioner is one of approximately 20'000 beneficiaries of Fondazione FAR, which finances early retirement in the construction industry. After an attack on the institution's IT partner, all beneficiaries were notified by letter.
The list also includes salary, retirement assets and partners' data. The people potentially affected number approximately 112'000, including former federal councillors.
In both incidents, the hackers did not target the pension funds directly, but rather the companies that provide their software. For Publica, the provider is PK Softech, a company from Reinach (BL) that has been active for over twenty years. Its clients include the two pension funds of the Canton of Bern, with over 92'000 insured persons, the Post Office pension fund, with 67'000, and the Migros pension fund, with 75'500.
Pension funds hold complete identities, AHV numbers, income and pension assets.
The institutions' responses differ. Publica and Fondazione FAR immediately notified the insured persons. The Post Office pension fund says the data was anonymized and that, at present, there is no need to take action; Migros is investigating. Both promise to inform any affected individuals. PK Softech is making no further statements. ## The risk lies in concentration
The most relevant element for insured persons is not only the breach of a single pension fund, but where it occurs. In the case described, the attack comes through the IT partner that supplies the software. The common provider thus becomes a point of concentration: a breach can potentially expose the data of multiple institutions in a single attack.
The difference compared with a direct attack is concrete. The pension fund may discover the problem and notify its members, but the technical perimeter also includes other clients of the same company. This is why Fondazione FAR, Publica, the Bernese pension funds, Posta and Migros appear together in the case: not because the source describes a single theft from all of them, but because the provider links multiple pension databases. The presence of the Confederation, Cantons, Posta and Migros therefore takes the case beyond a single administration or company. This distinction prevents a potential risk from being turned into an already confirmed breach.
### Data that make the contact credible
If salary, retirement assets and partners' data are added, the material enables criminals to prepare more plausible communications. The source also points to a selection criterion: target the wealthiest people, often elderly and therefore more vulnerable. The problem therefore concerns the combination of the data, not just the individual telephone number. The reference to the AVS number directly concerns previdenza AVS, while salary and retirement assets show why a pension fund is an attractive target.
The institutions' different responses also produce different scenarios for insured persons. An immediate notification, such as that from FAR and Publica, informs those who may be involved. The absence of evidence declared in Bern does not rule out involvement; the anonymization indicated by Posta reduces, according to the fund, the need to act immediately; Migros' checks leave the assessment open. In all cases, being potentially involved does not amount, in the source's text, to a theft already attributed to every insured person.

## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## A procedure based on the communications received
Anyone who receives a notice can follow a simple sequence, without confusing the levels of certainty indicated by the different institutions.
1. Read the communication from your pension fund and keep it. FAR wrote to all its approximately 20'000 beneficiaries after the attack on its IT partner. Publica notified all insured persons. These letters are the reference for understanding which incident is being reported and which data are indicated.
2. Distinguish the listed data from assumptions. In Publica's case, the source refers to data presumably stolen and lists name, date of birth, AVS number, address, telephone, e-mail, marital status, salary, retirement assets and partners' data. The list should not be turned into automatic confirmation for every person or every fund linked to PK Softech.
3. If you receive a call similar to the one received by the pensioner from central Switzerland, do not provide anything. The documented signs are a female voice, flawless Swiss German and the French prefix 0033. The pensioner had already received the notice from their fund and did not provide any data to the caller.
4. Await the institution's update. In Bern, the letters will arrive on Thursday; the fund says it cannot rule out involvement. Both have promised to inform any affected persons.
### A separate check for salary
Salary is among the information potentially involved in the Publica case, along with retirement assets and partners' data. Therefore, when rereading the documentation from your fund or busta paga svizzera, it is advisable to stick to the information actually received, without attributing to a letter content that the source does not indicate.
The incident shows that the communication procedure is still ongoing: some institutions wrote immediately, one announces letters for Thursday, one currently rules out the need to act and another is checking. The most concrete course of action therefore remains the documented one: read the notice, do not provide data in response to suspicious calls and await information from the institution when it promises to contact those concerned. ## TL;DR - Keller-Sutter launches the No campaign in Bern. - The vote by the people and the cantons is scheduled for November 29. - On March 8, 2026, 54,2% approved individual taxation. - The FDF challenges the coexistence of two tax systems.
## Key facts - Subject of the proposal: to make federal taxes fair for married couples and put an end to marriage discrimination - Date of the vote: November 29 - Approval of individual taxation: March 8, 2026 - Result: 54,2% in favor - Tax concerned: direct federal tax (IFD) - Conference venue: Bern - Possible decrease in revenue: between 680 million and three billion francs
Following popular approval of the switch to individual taxation on March 8, 2026, with 54,2% in favor, Karin Keller-Sutter launched the No campaign in Bern against the initiative aimed at guaranteeing fair federal taxes for married couples and putting an end to marriage discrimination; the people and the Cantons will vote on November 29.
The Federal Councillor, head of the Federal Department of Finance and spokesperson for the government's position, considers the proposed constitutional amendment outdated following the March decision. The reasoning is straightforward: the system approved by the people should not coexist with a second tax system for married couples.
The content of the proposal is explicit: for the IFD, married couples should continue to be taxed jointly as an economic unit, with a constitutional guarantee that they will not receive less favorable treatment than cohabiting couples.
### The issue of the two systems
“We do not want two separate tax systems in parallel,” Keller-Sutter said at a press conference in Bern. In her view, their coexistence would produce a worrying and complicated scenario. The minister acknowledged that constitutional law takes precedence over ordinary law, but stressed that the initiative concerns only direct federal tax (IFD).
Following the March vote, individual taxation will have to enter into force in the Cantons and municipalities in 2032. If the Centre's proposal were approved, however, this system could not be applied at federal level.
Parliament would have to take another decision to avoid the simultaneous application of two systems. The implementing legislation could then be challenged by referendum. Keller-Sutter described the risk as an endless discussion, a perpetuum mobile, arguing that a solution had already been reached after March 8.
The minister added that the Cantons, although they had opposed individual taxation, now do not want the coexistence of two systems. They would have to move forward with implementation at cantonal and municipal level without knowing whether, following a possible acceptance of the initiative, the federal model would actually be introduced. Keller-Sutter also expressed skepticism about the possibility that Parliament would abolish individual taxation after popular approval. To find one's bearings, the first distinction is not between one family and another, but between the levels of taxation. The initiative concerns the DFT; the individual taxation approved by the people must instead be implemented, after the March vote, at cantonal and municipal level in 2032. A possible yes vote on the initiative would alter the federal path, while the cantons would have to continue preparing their own transition without certainty about the next steps at national level.
### The comparison between the levels
| Level | Path indicated | |---|---| | DFT | The proposal maintains joint taxation; with a yes vote, individual taxation could not be introduced at federal level. | | Cantons and municipalities | Individual taxation must enter into force in 2032; the coexistence of the systems creates uncertainty. |
The second dimension concerns the family. The initiative wants spouses to continue to be taxed jointly as an economic unit for the DFT and not be treated less favourably than cohabiting couples. The FDF's position reverses the criterion: according to Keller-Sutter, the solution would ultimately favour married couples, whereas the state should not judge marital status through tax law. For those in a couple, the comparison is not limited to the outcome of the calculation alone: it concerns the relationship between marriage, cohabitation and methods of taxation.
For Keller-Sutter, in dual-income couples, joint taxation can discourage both spouses from increasing their employment rate. The second income earner is, in most cases, a woman: the tax obstacles associated with that income can weaken both spouses' financial independence, undermining their retirement security in old age and financial protection in the event of divorce. Equality between women and men is also more difficult to achieve as a result.
The method remains undecided. Parliament could choose full splitting, partial splitting or an alternative tax calculation. The latter would simulate joint and individual taxation, then apply the lower amount to the spouses. Until the model is chosen, it is not possible to determine a precise amount for each couple. The source nevertheless indicates a possible decline in revenue ranging from 680 million to three billion francs, depending on parliamentary decisions.

## TL;DR - TAF overturns Swisscom's 18 million fine - Comco had imposed conditions and a penalty - The judgment concerns the expansion of the fiber-optic network - An appeal to the Federal Supreme Court remains possible
## Key facts - Location → St. Gallen - Authority → Federal Administrative Court - Amount → 18 million francs - Technology → transition from P2P to P2MP - Judgment → September 21, 2026 - Comco investigation → late 2020 - Sanction decision → December 4, 2023 - Status → judgment not yet final
ST. GALLEN - The Federal Administrative Court (FAC) has upheld Swisscom's appeal in the dispute over the expansion of the fiber-optic network and annulled the decision by which the Competition Commission (Comco) had fined the company 18 million francs. In the market under examination, Swisscom does not hold a dominant position.
The FAC considers that Comco incorrectly applied cartel law. The measures ordered by the Commission also concerned areas where Swisscom had not yet begun expanding the network. Since it could not offer services in those areas, the judges held that the operator could not hold a dominant position either.
### From P2P to P2MP The case arose at the beginning of 2020, when Swisscom announced the switch from the point-to-point architecture, referred to as P2P, to the point-to-multipoint architecture, or P2MP. Under the previous system, each connection was linked directly to the central office via a dedicated fiber, which could also be leased by competing operators.
The new configuration instead provides for a shared line up to an intermediate distributor. From that point, the signal is split among the various connections. For other telecommunications providers, the change entails using Swisscom's signal and technology. The issue concerns the fiber network; to keep this dossier distinct from the other telephone services, the guide to telefonia mobile is also available.
At the end of 2020, Comco opened an investigation and adopted provisional measures to block installation of the new technology. After the FAC dismissed Swisscom's appeals in 2021, the Federal Supreme Court dismissed them in turn in 2022. On December 4, 2023, in the main proceedings, Comco imposed conditions for continuing the expansion and levied the penalty. The judgment of September 21, 2026, annuls that decision, but it can still be appealed before the Federal Supreme Court. ## What changes in practice The decision does not focus solely on the fine. The decisive point is how the relevant market is defined: the TAF's assessment depends on the technology present in a given area and on whether Swisscom can offer services through that network.
### Comparison between the two architectures | Element | P2P | P2MP | |---|---|---| | Connection | Dedicated fiber between the subscriber and the exchange | Shared line to an intermediate distributor | | Competitors' access | The fiber could be leased | Other providers use Swisscom's signal and technology | | Market considered by Comco | Dedicated and continuous connections | These connections no longer exist in the new configuration |
The distinction gives rise to two scenarios described in the judgment. In areas where the expansion had not yet begun, the TAF holds that Swisscom could not have held a dominant position: without the possibility of offering services, according to the judges, the condition identified by Comco was missing. In areas already equipped with the P2MP system, by contrast, the Court states that Swisscom does not operate in the market defined by the Commission, because that market essentially comprises dedicated and continuous fiber connections between the exchange and the buildings.
For telecommunications operators, the transition from P2P to P2MP therefore changes the technical relationship with the network. Previously, there was a dedicated fiber that could be leased; afterward, other providers must use Swisscom's signal and technology. The source does not, however, indicate any changes in prices, contracts, speeds or the work schedule for individual connections. The judgment annuls Comco's decision, but does not announce a commercial change for anyone using a fiber connection.
The proceedings also remain open judicially. Since the judgment has not yet become final, a possible appeal to the Federal Supreme Court could reopen the discussion. Also, to distinguish this matter concerning the fixed-line network from other services, the reference to telefonia mobile should be considered separately.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the case To correctly understand the effects of the judgment, it is useful to follow a precise sequence. The source does not indicate a new technical deadline for the expansion or an individual procedure for users; the relevant steps therefore concern the technology, the state of the network and the judicial process.
### Five checks 1. Identify the architecture mentioned: P2P means a dedicated connection between the user and the central office, while P2MP indicates a shared line up to an intermediate distributor. 2. Check the status of the expansion in the area concerned. The judgment distinguishes between areas where Swisscom had not yet begun the work and areas already equipped with P2MP. 3. Separate the market defined by Comco from the rest of the network. The Commission's reference essentially concerns dedicated, continuous fiber connections between the central office and buildings. 4. Reconstruct the dates of the proceedings: investigation at the end of 2020, appeals rejected in 2021 and 2022, main decision of December 4, 2023, and TAF judgment of September 21, 2026. 5. Still consider the judicial outcome provisional. The judgment is not final and binding and may be appealed before the Federal Supreme Court.
This sequence avoids confusing three different aspects: the network's technical model, the market definition used by Comco and the final validity of the TAF decision. For those following the case, the most concrete point is not a new tariff, which is not indicated in the source, but the criterion used by the judges to rule out Swisscom's dominant position.
The distinction between a network already using P2MP and a network not yet expanded is also decisive. In the first case, according to the TAF, Swisscom does not operate in the market defined by Comco; in the second, it cannot offer services and therefore cannot hold a dominant position. The situation can be changed only by a possible appeal before the Federal Supreme Court.

## Key facts - Body → Economic Affairs and Taxation Committee of the Council of States - Vote → 7 in favor, 2 against and 3 abstentions - Dossier → Council of States during the winter session - Working from home → maximum window from 14 to 17 hours; rest period from 11 to 9 hours - Disconnection → explicit right provided for by the National Council; CET-S wants to strike it - Sundays → maximum 5 hours without authorization, up to 9 Sundays a year
BERN - The competent committee of the Council of States has aligned itself with the National Council in supporting more flexible rules for working from home. Its support does not, however, extend to the entire bill: it wants to amend the provisions concerning disconnection and Sunday work.
### The bill under discussion A year ago, at the end of a heated debate, the People's Chamber had increased from 14 to 17 hours the maximum window within which the working day may be carried out. The minimum rest period, however, should be reduced from 11 to 9 hours. The National Council's text also provided for an explicit right to disconnect for all employees, not limited to those who work from home or outside their company.
CET-S, that is, the Economic Affairs and Taxation Committee of the Council of States, intends to remove the right to disconnect from the bill. According to the prevailing view in the committee, this protection would be guaranteed even without an explicit statutory provision.
Sunday work also divides the two chambers. The National Council intends to allow, without authorization, a maximum of five hours of work on no more than nine Sundays per year. The committee of the Council of States, on the other hand, proposes deleting the provision entirely, as a compromise, leaving the current restrictions in force.
The bill received 7 votes in favor, 2 against and 3 abstentions from CET-S in the overall vote. The Council of States will examine it during the winter session. In the People's Chamber, the groups of the Swiss People's Party, The Centre, the Radical Liberals and the Green Liberals had voted in favor.
For the majority, the bill updates labor legislation to current conditions while maintaining health protections. The Social Democratic Party and the Greens, on the other hand, fear a deterioration in working conditions, weaker health protection, an unnecessary increase in bureaucracy and insufficient consideration for solutions agreed between the social partners and for those specific to individual sectors. The source puts less strict rules for teleworking on the table, but indicates a different approach to disconnection and Sunday work. In the National Council's text, the right to disconnect would be set out in writing and would apply to everyone, not only to those who work from home or outside their own company. The second point is measurable. The National Council's proposal indicates a maximum of five hours without authorization and up to nine Sundays per year. ### Topics presented in Bern
In Bern, in front of the media, the promoters presented the arguments in support of the text. Representatives of the Swiss Animal Protection (SPA), other wildlife organisations, gamekeepers and farmers were present. The initiative aims to put limits on the use and sale of noisy pyrotechnic articles, in order to protect people, animals and the environment.
According to the promoters, domestic, income and wild animals have a hearing that is significantly more sensitive than human hearing. The sudden explosions of the fireworks display provoke fear, stress and panic. Those who take care of them, they add, must stay home with them on August 1 and New Year's Eve or get away from the shooting sites.
On August 1, 2026, Andrea Schaller, head of PSA in French-speaking Switzerland and Ticino, gave a concrete example. Due to the heatwave and severe drought, private lighting of fires had been prohibited on a large scale. On that day, he recalled, "not a single missing dog report was recorded." Normally, he added, calls during the National Day skyrocket.
For Schaller, the ban on firecrackers and other private pyrotechnic items would allow owners to organize with greater predictability: they would know when the official shows are scheduled and would not fear unpredictable noises from all sides. The geographical reference therefore encompasses the entire list in the report and, in the opponents’ view, links the criticism to the organization of production.

In view of the November 29 vote, the Federal Council and Parliament recommend rejecting the Centre's initiative «Enough with marriage discrimination». For direct federal tax, the text provides for maintaining joint taxation of married couples, who should not receive less favorable treatment than unmarried couples.
The proponents' proposal is limited to this level of taxation, but contains two elements. The first is confirmation of joint taxation for married couples. The second is an alternative calculation method, whereby the tax authorities would automatically apply the tax amount most advantageous for the couple.
The text therefore places the comparative treatment of couples at the forefront: it calls for married people to remain subject to joint taxation and for the result not to be less favorable than that for unmarried couples. The section on automatic calculation complements this request by indicating how the amount should be determined.

Karin Keller-Sutter, the Federal Councillor responsible for the Department of Finance, considers the proposal obsolete. The reason given is the move to individual taxation, approved by the people in March 2026. For the Federal Councillor, this move makes the Centre's proposal obsolete.
The Government raises both a financial and an institutional objection. In its view, approval would introduce different systems between the Confederation and the cantons. In addition, tax revenue could decrease by a maximum of three billion francs per year, depending on how it is implemented.

item.description: Press release published on October 13, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Press release published on October 13, 2026. - Influenza: recommended for people at high risk. - National Weeks: from November 2 to 7 and from November 23 to 28, 2026. - FOPH collaborates with CMB, FMH and pharmaSuisse.
## Key facts - Publication → 13 October 2026 - Influenza period → from mid-October to the beginning of the influenza wave - National weeks → from 2 to 7 and from 23 to 28 November 2026 - Vaccinations → influenza, COVID-19 and RSV - Promoters → CMB, FMH, pharmaSuisse and UFSP
### The situation announced in Bern The press release published in Bern on 13 October 2026 notes that the incidence of respiratory diseases is high during the winter half-year. Viruses and bacteria can affect the upper respiratory tract, bronchi and lungs. In Switzerland, influenza, RSV and COVID-19 cause thousands of hospital admissions every winter. Symptoms may begin mildly, resembling a cold, and then progress to a severe course. Vaccination against these diseases is therefore recommended for people at high risk.
Compared with the previous season, the recommendation against influenza remains unchanged. Those against COVID-19 and RSV, however, have been slightly modified.
In particular, vaccination against influenza is recommended for people aged 65 and over, pregnant women, people suffering from chronic diseases and children born prematurely between six months and two years of age. The infection can cause otitis media, pneumonia or myocarditis and, in some cases, neurological complications. In Switzerland, the most suitable window for vaccination runs from mid-October until the beginning of the influenza wave, generally expected between mid-December and mid-March.
### COVID-19 and RSV
For COVID-19, vaccination is indicated from September for people aged 65 and over, people with certain underlying conditions or trisomy 21, and pregnant women with certain underlying conditions. For pregnant women without underlying conditions, however, there is no longer a systematic recommendation.
During the winter half-year, an RSV infection is the most common cause of hospital admission among newborns and infants. To protect them during their first winter after birth, vaccination during pregnancy or immunization of the newborn after delivery may be used. Vaccination is still recommended from age 75; in the presence of certain underlying conditions, the recommendation starts at age 65, while for people with serious underlying conditions and a very high risk of severe disease, it is already provided from age 18.
This year, the supply of some influenza vaccines is delayed both in Switzerland and in the rest of Europe. The press release nevertheless guarantees that everyone who wishes to do so will be able to get vaccinated before the beginning of the influenza wave. Detailed recommendations and epidemiological figures updated weekly are available at www.vaccinare-svizzera.ch. For a separate in-depth look at LAMal/cassa malati, Frontaliere Ticino provides a dedicated guide. ## Three calendars for three recommendations
The practical reading of the press release begins with a distinction: there is only one winter season, but time windows and categories do not coincide. Influenza vaccination falls between mid-October and the beginning of the wave, while for COVID-19 the recommendation for people at high risk starts in September. For RSV, timing depends on the objective: protecting the child during the first winter after birth or reducing the risk of severe illness in the people indicated.
| Disease | Source indication | Timing or method | |---|---|---| | Influenza | Age 65, pregnancy, chronic diseases, prematurity between 6 months and 2 years | From mid-October to the beginning of the wave | | COVID-19 | Age 65, underlying conditions or trisomy 21; pregnancy with underlying conditions | Starting in September | | RSV | Protecting the child during the first winter; age 75; age 65 with underlying conditions; age 18 with severe conditions and very high risk | Vaccination during pregnancy or immunization after birth; vaccination for the indicated groups |
### What changes for families and older adults Pregnancy does not lead to a single indication applicable to all three viruses. For influenza, it is among the situations for which vaccination is recommended. For COVID-19, in contrast, the systematic recommendation no longer applies to pregnant women without underlying conditions, while it remains for those with certain conditions. For RSV, vaccination during pregnancy is one of the two options for protecting the child during the first winter after birth; the other is immunization after birth.
Age must also be considered alongside the disease. Age 65 is an explicit threshold for influenza and COVID-19. For RSV, the general recommendation starts at age 75, drops to age 65 in the presence of certain underlying conditions and reaches age 18 in cases of severe conditions and very high risk. The three vaccinations therefore have different target groups.
The National Weeks in November offer a common access point: from November 2 to 7 and from November 23 to 28, 2026, interested people can receive advice and access all three vaccinations at participating medical practices and pharmacies. For a separate pathway on LAMal/cassa malati, the website offers a dedicated guide.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## From recommendation to vaccination
The operational pathway starts from a single source: www.vaccinare-svizzera.ch. The portal collects complete information on all vaccinations recommended in Switzerland and allows users to consult the detailed recommendations. The figures and epidemiological data are updated weekly.
### Four operational steps 1. Consult the portal and read the information on influenza, COVID-19 and RSV. 2. Compare your situation with the indicated criteria: age, pregnancy, underlying conditions, trisomy 21 or premature birth when relevant. 3. Choose the correct window: COVID-19 from September onward, influenza from mid-October and before the wave, RSV during pregnancy or after childbirth to protect the child. 4. During the National Weeks, from November 2 to 7 and from November 23 to 28, 2026, contact a medical practice or participating pharmacy to receive advice and access vaccinations.
For influenza, delays in the supply of some vaccines concern Switzerland and all of Europe. The guarantee stated in the press release is that everyone who wishes to do so will be able to get vaccinated before the start of the influenza wave. The best period remains from mid-October to the beginning of the wave, usually expected in Switzerland between mid-December and mid-March.
The initiative is promoted by Collegio di medicina di base, in collaboration with FMH, pharmaSuisse and UFSP. For questions about the Vaccination Weeks, the press release indicates CMB at +41 31 370 06 70 and khm@hin.ch. The contact details for the pharmaSuisse media service are also available at +41 31 978 58 27 and medien@pharmaSuisse.org. The portal also contains an area for healthcare professionals with basic specialist knowledge and downloadable information material.
To complete the process with a reference on LAMal/cassa malati, consult the dedicated guide.
