item.title: Women-men income gap: falls to 14%
item.description: The income gap declines from 55% to 14% between generations.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The income gap falls from 55% to 14% across generations. - In 2025, tertiary qualification: 54% of women versus 48% of men. - The difference in hours worked falls from 17 to less than four. - Among parents, the income gap remains at 51%.
## Key facts - Study → published in the journal «Social Change in Switzerland» - Authors → Daniel Oesch and Oliver Lipps - Sample → over 215'000 people aged 25 to 34 - Data → Swiss labour force surveys from 1991 to 2024 - Generation analyzed → people born in 1995 - Overall gap → 14% - Education in 2025 → 54% of young women and 48% of young men with tertiary qualifications - Gap between parents → 51%
## The central finding comes from Lausanne
Among people born in 1995 in Switzerland, the gap in earned income between women and men remains 14%. This is shown by a study by the University of Lausanne and the competence centre for social sciences Fors, published on Tuesday in the journal «Social Change in Switzerland».
The clearest comparison is between people born in 1965 and those born in 1995. For the first generation, women earned 55% less than men overall. Among those born in 1995, the difference had narrowed to 14%. The researchers describe this development as a «race to catch up».
The change also concerns hours worked and hourly wages. The difference in weekly working hours fell from 17 hours to less than four. The gap between standardized hourly wages narrowed from almost 20% to less than 5%.
The growth in women's education is cited as one of the factors that contributed to this development. In 2025, 54% of young women in Switzerland had obtained a tertiary qualification, compared with 48% of young men. In addition, more women enter professions with better salary prospects.
The improvement is also evident in comparison with France, Sweden, Great Britain and the United States. Switzerland went from having the second-highest income gap among people born in 1965 to the smallest for the 1995 generation. To explore the relationship between income and personal circumstances in greater depth, the study can be read alongside a calcolatore stipendio. ## How to read the gap
### Three measures to keep separate
For people who live and work in Switzerland, the first practical way to read the data is not to mix different indicators. The study presents the overall income-from-work gap, but also measures the difference in weekly working hours and in standardized hourly wages. These are three related aspects in describing the phenomenon, but they do not represent the same thing.
The shift from a 17-hour difference to less than four shows that weekly working hours carry less weight than in previous generations. The decline in the hourly wage gap, from almost 20% to less than 5%, instead indicates a change in wage conditions. The overall reduction in income from work, from 55% to 14%, must therefore be read together with the other two figures, without using a single indicator to describe the whole situation.
Education offers a second way of reading the data. In 2025, young women with a tertiary education qualification accounted for 54%, compared with 48% of young men. The source links the rising level of women's education to the observed trend and also points to access to professions with greater salary prospects. This does not, however, coincide with the disappearance of differences, especially when family life comes into play.
### The point that changes with children
The comparison between people without children and parents radically changes the picture. For people without children, the gender gap fell from 27% in the 1965 generation to 7% in the 1995 generation. Among parents, however, the difference remains at 51%. This figure makes it risky to apply the average improvement to all individual situations.
The international comparison should also be used as a reference, not as a substitute for personal analysis. France, Sweden, Great Britain and the United States provide the benchmark chosen by the researchers: Switzerland has moved from a very unfavorable position to having the smallest gap. Anyone considering a career change can consult annunci di lavoro, keeping education, working hours, hourly wages and family situation separate.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## A practical framework for using the data
### Four reading steps
1. Start with the right indicator. Before comparing two situations, determine whether you are looking at total labor income, weekly hours, or standardized hourly wage. The study uses all these measures and shows that they can move together without being identical.
2. Consider the generation. The results mainly compare people born in 1965 and 1995, while the sample concerns people between 25 and 34 years old. The percentages therefore describe generational groups analyzed by the researchers, not an automatic result for every individual female worker or every individual male worker.
3. Include family status as a separate item. The shift from 27% to 7% for people without children and the figure of 51% among parents show that parenthood changes the comparison. It is not enough to stop at the average of 14% referring to the 1995 generation.
4. Read education together with occupation. The 54% of young women with tertiary qualifications, compared with 48% of young men, signals an educational change. The source adds that more women enter occupations with greater salary prospects, but specifies that education and salary gains are not enough to close inequalities linked to family life.
After these steps, the most accurate comparison keeps the data on hours, hourly wage, total income and the presence of children side by side. The international reference also remains readable only by indicating the group of countries chosen by the study: France, Sweden, Great Britain and the United States.
This framework makes it possible to use the figures without turning them into an individual promise. The improvement between generations is documented, but the gap remains particularly pronounced among parents. To compare your own salary, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Franc strengthens against the euro: Stucki’s forecasts
item.description: Stucki sees the franc stronger against the euro by the end of the year The exchange rate has fallen from 95 to 93 centimes The French deficit is about 5% of GDP The SNB should not
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Stucki sees the franc stronger against the euro by year-end - The exchange rate fell from 95 to 93 cents - France's deficit is about 5% of GDP - The SNB should not change interest rates immediately
## Key facts - Expert → Thomas Stucki, head of investments at St. Gallen Cantonal Bank - Source → interview published by the Cash portal - Exchange rate → the euro fell from 95 to 93 cents - France → budget deficit close to 5% of gross domestic product - Nominal growth → 1.9% - Inflation → 1% in September - US rates → ten-year yield reached 5.25% - Next rate increase → expected only for next year
Thomas Stucki, head of investments at St. Gallen Kantonalbank, expects the franc to strengthen against the euro by the end of the year. The warning, reported by ATS, comes after a new phase of tension on the European bond market, which has rekindled doubts about debts, budget discipline and structural divergences in the Eurozone.
The euro, explains the expert in the interview published by the Cash portal, had been able to present itself as an alternative to the dollar for large investors intending to reduce exposure to the American currency. Now the same operators are being reminded that the fundamental problems of the Eurozone have not been solved.
The tension was reflected in the gearbox. In a short time, the Swiss currency appreciated and the euro rate dropped from 95 to 93 cents, before stopping temporarily. For Stucki, the first reaction has passed; the breadth of the movement also depends on the surprise of many bulls on the euro. A return to summer levels of strength appears unlikely, as the French issue will remain under observation.
### France and Swiss rates
French finance is the most delicate point of the analysis. The budget deficit is around 5% of gross domestic product, while the nominal growth of the economy reaches just 1.9%. The debt/GDP ratio is therefore destined to rise and, according to Stucki, there is no political will to adopt austerity measures. Ahead of next year's presidential elections, populist parties at opposite ends are instead promising to hand out more money. The youth protests and the government's impotence, he adds, do not communicate the image of a stable and reliable debtor.
By the end of the year, the forecast is for the euro to be weaker than current levels but still above 0.90 francs.
> «Our forecast remains unchanged: we had already considered the euro's rise to almost 95 cents unsustainable».
The strengthening of the franc reduces the price of imported goods and helps to contain inflation, but the speed of the movement still poses a danger to the SNB. With inflation at 1% in September, prices remain in line with the objectives of the institute directed by Martin Schlegel, so there is currently no reason to change rates. According to Stucki, the SNB should sooner or later leave rates at zero: the next step should be a hike, while the first tightening is only expected next year and will depend on the trend in rates abroad. ## Practical impact for Switzerland
The move from 95 to 93 cents shows how quickly the euro-franc exchange rate can change when investors seek a safe haven. For people living in Switzerland, the consequence identified by the source is seen in imported goods: a stronger franc lowers their cost and can help curb inflation. It provides support for the cost of living, not a promise that every price will fall immediately or by the same amount.
The other side concerns the SNB. Inflation at 1% in September remains compatible with its objectives, but a rapid appreciation of the franc is described as a greater and more likely risk than a weakening. The bank must therefore weigh two signals together: lower import costs help keep prices down, while sudden demand for the franc shows that currency conditions can change quickly. For a Swiss budget, the benefit of lower import costs coexists with exchange-rate uncertainty.
### Three interpretations not to conflate
| Signal | What the source indicates | | --- | --- | | Stronger franc | Lower cost of imported goods and support for containing inflation | | First SNB hike | Expected only next year, with timing dependent on foreign interest rates | | US yields at 5,25% | No widespread flight from stocks so far |
The table separates observations and expectations. As for the exchange rate, the year-end estimate remains that the euro will be weaker than current levels but above 90 cents. As for interest rates, Stucki does not see an imminent turning point. These are different horizons: the first concerns the value of the currency, the second the cost of money.
Stock markets also require a less mechanical interpretation. The move above 5% in ten-year US government bond yields has not so far triggered a widespread flight from stocks; yields reached 5,25%. For Stucki, there is no threshold that automatically moves investors into bonds. The greater risk would be a rapid and uncontrolled increase, a sign of fear about the economic stability of the United States. Investments in artificial-intelligence infrastructure continue to support stock indexes. To track the effect on costo della vita in Svizzera, pair the exchange-rate data with the price data. The comparatore CHF/EUR makes it possible to observe the relationship between the two currencies.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## Operational checklist
The source does not indicate an administrative deadline or a single procedure. For those who need to find their bearings in Swiss economic life, the possible action is a three-step check, anchored to the timing and signals cited by Stucki.
### 1. Separate observed exchange rate and forecast
First, record the level you are looking at and compare it with the two points indicated by the source: the euro had fallen from 95 to 93 cents, and the year-end forecast keeps it above 90. Use the comparatore CHF/EUR to read the ratio without confusing a market change with an SNB decision. The forecast is not a guarantee: the movement also depends on tensions in the bond market and the situation in France.
### 2. Check the effect on the budget
In the second step, separate items related to imported goods from other expenses. According to the source, a strong franc reduces the cost of imports and helps contain inflation; the check is therefore intended to understand where the effect may be visible, without automatically attributing every change to the exchange rate. To compare the impact on spending, use the costo della vita in Svizzera. The 1% inflation reading in September does not by itself warrant forecasting an immediate change in interest rates.
### 3. Keep the two horizons distinct
On the monetary front, consider the present and next year separately. Stucki does not anticipate an imminent shift; the first tightening is expected only next year and will depend on interest rates abroad. There is therefore no need to base a decision on a more precise date, because the source does not provide one. The check to repeat concerns the evolution of foreign interest rates and the speed of the franc’s strengthening.
### 4. Read the stock markets beyond the threshold
On the financial side, the correct check is not to ask whether the US 10-year yield has surpassed 5%: it has already reached 5.25% without a generalized flight from equities. The question indicated by the source instead concerns the speed and intensity of the increase. A disruptive event, comparable to the shock of the tariffs announced by President Donald Trump in April 2025, would be the scenario necessary for a jolt of that kind. Investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure meanwhile remain a source of positive news for market indexes.
This sequence avoids mixing exchange rates, prices, interest rates and stocks. To translate the different scenarios into your own budget, use the calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.description: ASI has submitted 100'848 signatures to the Federal Chancellery The appeal calls for the counterproposal to be withdrawn The project concerns the review of rents
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - ASI delivered 100'848 signatures to the Federal Chancellery - The appeal calls for the counterproposal to be withdrawn - The proposal concerns the review of rents and a rent based on costs - According to the initiative, excessive rents should be reduced automatically
## Key facts - Who → Swiss Tenants' Association (ASI) - Where → Federal Chancellery, Bern - Signatures → 100'848 - Federal Council decision → September 25 - Request → halt work on the counterproposal - Duration of collection → two weeks
## The handover in Bern 100'848 signatures were handed in today to the Federal Chancellery. The Swiss Tenants' Association (ASI) is asking the Federal Council to withdraw the counterproposal to the popular initiative «Yes to protection against excessive rents». The appeal also calls for work on the indirect counterproposal to be stopped immediately.
The Federal Council is having the draft prepared, which should address the review of rents and rent based on costs. On September 25, it had chosen to submit it as a response to the initiative promoted by ASI. Under that decision, the initial rent should be able to be aligned with that of comparable apartments in the area.
### The point contested by ASI For the association, however, the statistical benchmark would have the opposite effect to that sought by the initiative. Every higher new rent would end up in the reference rent, contributing, according to ASI, to further fueling the spiral of rental prices. The association also objects to the possibility of increases every four years and the absence of a review.
Jacqueline Badran, a Zurich Socialist National Councillor and member of the ASI committee, argues that the Federal Council is aiming for a market rent. In her view, this approach would conflict with the popular initiative, which should establish the principle of rent calculated based on costs and a maximum cap on returns.
For Carlo Sommaruga, president of ASI and member of the Council of States (PS/GE), tenants already bear excessive housing costs. Sommaruga interpreted the signature collection, completed in two weeks, as a clear response to the Federal Council.
The text of the protest therefore focuses on the relationship between the level of the initial rent and the criterion used to compare it. For ASI, a benchmark fueled by new increases would not correct rents, but would push them upwards. For those following the impact of rents on costo della vita in Svizzera, the debate now turns to the criterion chosen to determine the initial rent. ## Two approaches compared The divergence concerns not only the name of the counterproposal. It concerns how it is determined whether a rent is excessive and which parameter is used to set the initial rent. The source compares two approaches: on the one hand, an automatic review with a reduction when the rent is too high; on the other, an adjustment of the initial rent to that of similar apartments in the area.
| Point | Initiative | Counterproposal described | |---|---|---| | Correction | Review and reduction of excessively high rents | Adjustment of the initial rent to that of similar apartments | | Stated basis | Rent based on costs | Statistical reference rent |
The practical issue is the composition of the reference. ASI argues that every new, more expensive rent would enter it, with the risk of further fuelling the price spiral. In its view, the parameter could therefore incorporate precisely the increases it should help assess. The same association points out that increases would be possible every four years and that no verification would be provided for.
This means that the same expression, reference rent, carries a different weight in the two scenarios: for the Federal Council, it is the criterion for comparing similar dwellings; for ASI, it risks becoming a mechanism that records and fuels increases. The divergence is therefore not merely technical, but concerns the outcome expected by the tenant.
### Two scenarios for someone paying rent If the counterproposal were applied in the form described, the initial rent could be brought closer to that of similar dwellings. The element to observe would therefore be the area's statistical reference, together with the effects ASI attributes to it.
If, on the other hand, the initiative's approach prevailed, the starting point would be the automatic review and reduction of excessively high rents. Jacqueline Badran links this approach to upholding the principle of rent based on costs and the maximum cap on returns. These are scenarios in the political debate, not rules already presented by the source as operational.
The impact on the budget should be assessed starting from actual income: a busta paga svizzera provides the basis for personal comparison.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## What to do today if you are a tenant The news concerns a counterproposal currently being prepared. For anyone who pays rent, the useful step is not to anticipate a change to the contract, but to organize the data that makes it possible to follow the federal debate without confusing a proposal with the rules already applicable to rental agreements.
### A practical sequence 1. Retrieve the rental agreement and identify the initial rent. Record separately the current amount and any increase already communicated. The project described by the Federal Council starts precisely from the possibility of adjusting the initial rent to that of similar apartments in the area.
2. Build the comparison with similar dwellings, without turning a single listing into an average. The point contested by ASI is that every more expensive new rental could end up in the reference and fuel the price spiral.
3. If your interest is reducing rent that is too high, distinguish the initiative's criterion from the counterproposal's mechanism. In the first case, the request is an automatic review with a reduction; in the second, the reference is the initial rent of similar dwellings. This distinction prevents attributing to the current contract an effect that the source links only to the two political scenarios.
4. For communications already received from the landlord, separate the political discussion from the procedure currently in force: tenancy law is federal and the same in every Canton. A landlord's termination is valid only on the official cantonal form; if you want to contest it, the deadline is 30 days before the conciliation authority.
5. Check the deposit: it may not exceed three months' rent and must be held in a blocked account in the tenant's name. This check concerns the existing tenancy, not the statistical criterion being discussed for the future.
Follow the Federal Council's deliberations and ASI's positions. The signature-collection campaign calls for the withdrawal of the counterproposal, while the project remains in the preparation phase described by the source. Therefore, keep your rental documentation and update the comparison when the project is finalized.
### From personal data to the budget To estimate the effect of rent on income, start with your personal budget and separate the rent from the other monthly items. When the political text is clarified, maintain the same sequence: contract data, initial rent, increases already communicated, and reference to similar apartments. This way, you do not confuse ASI's proposal, the federal counterproposal, and your situation.

item.description: Suva saved 123 million in 2025 Approximately 2,9 million invoices checked 297'000 invoices had errors or inaccuracies Without the checks, average premiums
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Suva saved 123 million in 2025 - Approximately 2,9 million invoices checked - 297'000 invoices contained errors or inaccuracies - Without the checks, average company premiums about three percent higher
## Key facts - Year → 2025 - Headquarters → Lucerne - Audited invoices → approximately 2.9 million - Savings → 123 million francs - Treatment costs → 1.3 billion francs - Invoices with errors → 297,000 (10.4% of the total) - Unaudited premiums → approximately three percent higher on average - Automatic processing → three-quarters of invoices
In 2025, Suva saved 123 million francs by auditing approximately 2.9 million invoices. The accident insurer announced the results on Tuesday. Treatment expenditures amounted to 1.3 billion francs, 6% higher than the previous year.
### Auditing medical invoices
The audits focused on invoices for medical and therapeutic services. According to data released by Suva, 297,000 documents contained errors or inaccuracies, representing 10.4% of the total reviewed. Suva therefore returned these invoices for correction.
The press release notes, among other issues, duplicate charges, errors in billing, services without insurance coverage, and invoices for cases already closed. In some cases, there were also charges for services never performed. Overall, the examples concern billing, insurance coverage, and the actual provision of services.
Invoices for medical costs are digitally verified, and Suva automatically processes three-quarters of them. The press release therefore describes a check applied to medical and therapeutic service documents, with invoices being returned when errors or inaccuracies are discovered.
### The Link to Company Premiums
Michael Widmer, head of healthcare cost management at Suva, linked the audits to the premium levels of insured companies:
> "In the absence of such audits, the average premiums of insured companies would increase by approximately three percent."
The estimate refers to the average number of insured companies. Suva is headquartered in Lucerne and protects more than 2.2 million workers from the consequences of accidents and occupational diseases.
The numbers in the report use different units: 2.9 million refers to audited invoices, 297,000 to those with errors or inaccuracies, and over 2.2 million refers to insured workers. The savings are expressed in francs, the increase in healthcare costs as a percentage, and the effect on premiums as an estimated average. The comparison with the previous year concerns healthcare costs; it is not presented as an explanation for the anomalies found. The most useful figure for a practical reading is to separate the four aspects of the communication: the number of invoices checked, the share with errors, the total cost of treatment and the estimated average effect on the premiums of insured companies. These are different measures and do not make it possible to calculate how much each individual company saved.
### Four numbers, four meanings
| Indicator | Reported figure | Interpretation | |---|---|---| | Invoices checked | approximately 2,9 million | scope of the check | | Errors or inaccuracies | 297'000, amounting to 10,4% | invoices sent back for correction | | Treatment costs | 1,3 billion, +6% compared with the previous year | total reached in 2025 | | Premiums without checks | about 3% higher on average | estimate referring to insured companies |
The table compares what Suva checked, what it found and what it estimated as the effect on premiums. The 10,4% is not a percentage increase in treatment costs, while the +6% is not the share of erroneous invoices. The source does not attribute the +6% to a specific anomaly and does not indicate a savings amount per invoice.
### What changes in how premiums are read
For an insured company, the practical figure is an average estimate: without the checks, premiums would be about three percent higher. However, this is not a percentage applied in the text to every company, every sector or every invoice. The communication does not provide a breakdown for each individual contract, nor an individual calculation.
The difference between the two scenarios is therefore described at an aggregate level: on the one hand, the checks that produced savings of 123 million francs; on the other, the assumption of premiums being higher on average in the absence of the checks. The source does not establish that the two values are equivalent or that the 123 million turns into the same amount for a single company.
For people living in Switzerland, the news does not provide a personal premium or an amount to enter in the household budget. The reference to costo della vita in Svizzera therefore serves only to keep the aspects separate: here the source discusses invoices checked by Suva, treatment costs and the premiums of insured companies. It does not present a new individual tariff.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. Moving from general information to concrete verification requires not confusing invoices, the cost of care, and the company premium. The source allows for a limited but precise checklist: it clarifies the path of the invoices, but does not add an administrative procedure for the individual insured person.
### Checklist based on the reported data
1. Identify the reference year. The data concern 2025: approximately 2,9 million invoices checked and 123 million francs saved. 2. Separate the overall expenditure. Spending on care amounted to 1,3 billion francs, an increase of 6% over the previous year. This figure must not be confused with the premium of a single company. 3. Read the outcome of the check. Invoices with errors or inaccuracies numbered 297'000, equal to 10,4%, and were sent back to be corrected. The anomalies indicated include double billing, incorrect calculations, services not covered, cases already closed, and services never provided. 4. Distinguish the computerized check from its consequence. Suva processes three quarters of the invoices automatically; the source does not say that every document receives the same outcome, nor does it indicate a different procedure for each anomaly. 5. Use the estimate on premiums with caution. The roughly three percent figure refers to the average premiums of insured companies in the scenario without checks. It is not a personal amount that can be calculated for a worker or a single company.
The press release does not indicate a deadline for correction, a form, an office, or a division of the work among the parties involved. These details cannot be derived from the published figures. The only explicit operational step is that Suva sends back invoices with errors or inaccuracies so they can be corrected.
To put the items in one's own income into context without attributing to Suva a calculation that the source does not provide, one can consult the busta paga svizzera. The link does not replace Suva's data: it merely helps keep the personal picture separate from the average estimate referring to insured companies.
For a personal verification of salary items, use the calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Increase in mortgage rates in the third quarter of 2024
item.description: The cost of mortgages rose in the third quarter.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Mortgage costs rose in the third quarter. - The ten-year fixed rate was 2.07% at the end of September. - The five-year rate was 1.9%; the three-year rate was 1.75%. - The SNB kept the reference rate at 0%.
## Key facts - Period → third quarter - Survey → end of September - Ten-year fixed rate → 2,07% - Five-year fixed rate → 1,9% - Three-year fixed rate → 1,75%, compared with 1,38% three months earlier - SNB → reference rate at 0% - Basis for calculation → average of the rates of around thirty banks - Comparison service → Comparis
At the end of September, the indicative rate for a ten-year fixed-rate mortgage stood at 2,07% in Switzerland. The figure, calculated as the average of the rates of around thirty banks, is reported by Comparis in a note. The report is marked with the Keystone-ATS designation.
The five-year rate stood at 1,9%, while the three-year rate was 1,75%. For the latter term, the level was higher than three months earlier, when it was 1,38%. The figures cover the third quarter and confirm an increase in the cost of mortgages compared with the previous three months.
### The link with capital markets The source links the movement mainly to the increase in interest rates on capital markets. For banks, this drove up refinancing costs, with an impact on indicative rates for fixed-rate mortgages.
The trend in foreign interest rates continues to be transmitted to the Swiss capital market. The SNB's reference rate, however, remains at 0%, while indicative rates for ten-year fixed mortgages exceed 2%. The note therefore links the increase in fixed-rate mortgage costs to capital markets, not to an increase in the reference rate that has already taken place.
Dirk Renkert, real estate expert for Comparis, writes in the note:
Dirk Renkert, real estate expert for Comparis, observes in the note that, in the short term, still-contained inflation should prompt the SNB not to rush to raise interest rates. At the same time, the more favorable economic outlook, the weak franc and higher energy prices have increased the likelihood of monetary tightening.
The source thus describes a possible tightening of monetary policy, but puts the SNB reference rate at 0%. ## Comparing terms To understand the practical impact of the survey, the first criterion is to distinguish the mortgage term. The figures reported do not describe a single product: they compare three-, five-, and ten-year fixed-rate financing.
### One parameter at a time | Term | Indicative rate at end of quarter | Available comparison | |---|---:|---| | Three years | 1.75% | 1.38% three months earlier | | Five years | 1.9% | level indicated at end of quarter | | Ten years | 2.07% | level indicated at end of September |
The sequence shows that, in the survey, the indicative rate rises as one moves from the three-year term to the five-year term and then to the ten-year term. The comparison with three months earlier is specified for the three-year term: from 1.38% to 1.75%. For the other terms, the source provides the level observed at the end of the period under consideration.
The statistical basis matters. Since the figure is derived from the average of the rates of around thirty banks, it represents a market benchmark and not a single bank's figure. To compare two indications correctly, it is therefore necessary to verify that the term is the same and that both cases involve a fixed rate.
The second element to distinguish is the SNB rate from the mortgage rate. The fact that the central bank's benchmark remains at 0% does not automatically bring fixed-rate mortgages to the same level: the source attributes their increase to capital markets and banks' refinancing costs.
There is also the twofold interpretation indicated by Comparis: inflation still contained in the short term, but more favorable economic prospects, a weak franc, and rising energy prices increasing the likelihood of tightening. To complement the rate comparison with a budget check, one can consult the costo della vita in Svizzera and use the calcolatore stipendio as a guidance tool.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## A verification procedure Anyone considering a fixed-rate mortgage can turn the note into a comparison sheet without mixing different indicators. The procedure must remain anchored to the durations, periods and causes reported by the source.
### Five operational checks 1. Start with Comparis's online price comparison service, cited in the note, and identify the reference period: the third quarter, with data collected at the end of September. 2. Choose only one duration for each comparison: three, five or ten years. Do not place values referring to different maturities on the same level. 3. Report the indicative rate corresponding to the chosen duration. For the three-year term, also note the previous available comparison, at 1,38% three months earlier. 4. Keep the BNS reference rate, at 0%, separate from the price of the fixed-rate mortgage. These are quantities mentioned together by the source, but they do not coincide. 5. Complete the reading with the factors indicated by Comparis: foreign interest rates, the Swiss capital market, banks' refinancing costs, inflation, the franc and energy prices.
This framework prevents an indicative rate from being turned into an automatic forecast. Instead, it makes it possible to check whether the comparison concerns the same duration and the same type of financing. The time dimension is equally important: the three-year figure can also be read in relation to the preceding three months, while the end-of-period level remains the reference for the other reported values.
Before using the figures for a personal assessment, it is advisable to keep the market snapshot and your own situation separate. The note does not provide an individual offer or a decision already made by the BNS; it describes the indicative rates and the factors influencing their trend. To check your monthly margin, use calcolatore stipendio.

One thousand solar panels, tilted at 60 degrees, are at the centre of the project being carried out by Tunnel du Grand-St-Benard SA in Bourg-Saint-Pierre, on the Swiss side of the Great St Bernard. The system will cover the roof of the gallery providing access to the tunnel.
The decision was made to increase reliance on renewable energy. The planned total area is 7000 square metres; the text describes the panels as currently being installed.
### A schedule divided into tranches
The schedule proceeds in tranches. Installation of the thousand panels will begin at the end of 2026 and continue in 2027. The commissioning of approximately 3000 square metres is expected by the end of this year, while the remaining 4000 will be activated during the following year. Before moving to the installation phase, the company carried out a testing period between 2022 and 2025.
The expected result is stated precisely: 450 MWh of electricity produced each year, equal to half the tunnel's energy needs. The source therefore links the new production to the consumption of the tunnel's facilities.
> “We have a large flat roof area,” said Baptiste Cavin, engineer responsible for maintenance and projects at Tunnel du Grand-St-Bernard SA.
Cavin specified that the solar farm will provide a winter supplement to the production already available. Electricity demand covers lighting, electromechanical systems and ventilation, and is described as considerable.
The total cost of the work is approximately 2 million francs. The work is carried out by company employees, and the project is 100% in-house.
The source finally specifies that this project has no connection with the floating solar farm on Lac des Toules, located at an altitude of 1810 metres in Bourg-Saint-Pierre territory (VS) and belonging to the electricity company Romande Energie. This distinction clarifies the scope of the announcement: the project concerns the tunnel and its roof on the Swiss side. ## A practical look at the investment
The new plant is part of a renewable production system already operating at the company. Inside the tunnel, a hydroelectric power station operates, powered by a small dam built along the road to the Great St Bernard Pass.

The photovoltaic system is presented as a winter supplement to current production. item.description: Since February, gasoline has risen to 2,11 francs per liter 15'000 km annually and 6 l/100 km: 423 francs more Kerosene costs twice as much as last year
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Since February, petrol has risen to 2,11 francs per litre - 15'000 km per year and 6 l/100 km: 423 francs more - Kerosene costs twice as much as last year - Oil at 180 dollars could slow growth
## Key facts - Petrol → from 1,64 to 2,11 francs per litre - Annual increase → 423 francs for the specified TCS profile - Swiss flights → flights to Dubai resuming from October 27 - Kerosene → price doubled compared with last year - Oil → from 100 to 120 dollars: another 10-15 cents per litre - KOF scenario → oil at 180 dollars and inflation temporarily above 2%
Since February, petrol in Switzerland has risen from 1,64 to 2,11 francs per litre. The Touring Club Suisse figure translates the geopolitical crisis into an immediate expense: with 15'000 kilometres per year, average consumption of six litres per 100 kilometres and the indicated price, the additional outlay reaches 423 francs per year. Diesel and heating oil have recorded significant price increases since the start of the war in Iran, according to Avenergy.
### The bill already visible for motorists and travellers
For those considering a trip, the risk mainly concerns routes to Asia. To bypass several Middle Eastern airspaces and comply with the ban on overflying Russia, airlines have fewer alternatives. Longer routes increase consumption and costs, with possible repercussions for passengers. Following the Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport, Swiss has not announced any further changes and confirms the resumption of flights to Dubai from October 27.
The price of kerosene, explains aviation expert Hansjörg Bürgi, has already doubled compared with last year. Fuel accounts for around one third of airlines’ expenses: if carriers were to extend their routes further, fares could increase. The attacks also risk delaying Riyadh’s development as an international hub by years, to the benefit of Istanbul, Addis Ababa, Paris and London.
The risk is also reaching shops. If energy remains expensive for a long time, producing and transporting goods will cost more, potentially leading to price increases on shelves and renewed pressure on inflation. Jan-Egbert Sturm, director of KOF, considers Switzerland relatively well placed: it depends less on heavy industry than other European countries, and the strong franc eases the cost of energy imports. The phenomenon also affects costo della vita in Svizzera.
However, KOF points to a risk for exports: a global slowdown would reduce demand for Swiss products. In a scenario with oil at 180 dollars per barrel, growth could slow in the following year and inflation temporarily exceed 2%, while remaining below 2% on an annual average. For Marcus Schneider, the conflict is now a regional crisis; according to the political scientist, a full-scale escalation is already under way, and it remains to be seen how much worse it could become. ## Three scenarios for the Swiss portfolio
The most immediate figure is the TCS figure, but it is not a rate that is the same for everyone. The 423 francs are based on a specific profile: 15'000 kilometres per year, six litres per 100 kilometres and the jump from 1,64 to 2,11 francs per litre. The useful comparison for a family is therefore between its own mileage, average consumption and the indicated change, without automatically extending that result to every motorist.
### From the observed price increase to the future risk
The practical distinction is between what has already happened and what depends on how the crisis evolves. The source identifies three developments that can also be seen in day-to-day life:
| Scenario | Effect indicated in the source | | Oil from 100 to 120 dollars per barrel | Another 10-15 cents per litre at the pump | | Oil at 180 dollars per barrel | Weaker growth in the following year and inflation temporarily above 2% | | High energy prices for a long time | More expensive production and transport, with possible price increases on store shelves |
The first scenario is linked to new supply disruptions, while commodities expert Bekim Laski points out that, at the moment, a further surge is not the most likely scenario. The figure therefore serves as a stress threshold, not as an automatic forecast for every motorist.
For air tickets, the pressure stems from the combination of two costs: fuel and route distance. Any increase would not necessarily affect every flight, but the risk is more evident on routes to Asia, where avoided airspace and the ban on flying over Russia narrow the alternatives. The planned resumption of Swiss connections to Dubai from October 27 remains the announced reference point.
From an economic standpoint, the strong franc offers partial protection for energy imports, while lower dependence on heavy industry sets Switzerland apart from other European countries. The downside is foreign demand: if the global economy slows, Swiss exports may suffer. The comparatore CHF/EUR helps isolate the role of the exchange rate when assessing this factor.
Duration matters more than an isolated peak, according to Sturm. For this reason, a temporary rise in oil prices does not automatically amount to a recession: the KOF model indicates average annual inflation still below 2% in the scenario described, even if the threshold may be exceeded temporarily.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## A practical five-step check
Anyone who needs to organize their budget can separate costs already observed from scenarios that are still open. The method does not eliminate uncertainty, but it avoids confusing a TCS figure with an assumption about oil.
### From certain expenses to scenarios
1. Start with your consumption profile. List your annual kilometers and average consumption; then compare them with the reference used by TCS, 15'000 kilometers and six liters per 100. The value of 423 francs helps gauge the order of magnitude of the case described, not assign the same expense to every motorist.
2. Keep the price increases already reported separate. Gasoline, diesel and heating oil are the items identified as having already increased. For oil, instead, note separately the scenario of 100 to 120 dollars per barrel and the estimated effect of 10-15 cents per liter. It is a simulation linked to new supply disruptions, not a price announcement.
3. If you are considering a flight to Asia, consider the route in addition to the displayed price. Avoided airspace and the ban on flying over Russia can lengthen the journey. For Swiss, the source reports the planned resumption of connections with Dubai from October 27 and no further changes announced after the Houthi attacks against Riyadh airport.
4. For everyday spending, observe the link between energy, transport and store shelves. If energy prices remain high for a long time, the production and transport of goods may become more expensive. This is the step to follow when assessing costo della vita in Svizzera, without confusing the risk with a price increase already generalized across all products.
5. Finally, use the KOF scenario as an interpretive limit: oil at 180 dollars per barrel, weaker growth in the following year and inflation temporarily above 2%, but below 2% on an annual average. The global slowdown remains the channel that may hit demand for Swiss products and exports. A recession, however, is not automatic according to the reported analysis.
This sequence offers a concrete basis: measure your consumption, distinguish the increase already visible from the risk, check the route of a trip and assess the macroeconomic effect. To translate these items into your personal budget, use calcolatore stipendio/imposte.
